title: Convergence triage canvas
description: A reviewer sees every concurrent proposal as one comparable set on a single surface — cards, exact counts, the conflict map — with click-first interaction, honest first-load and failure states, and set freshness that converges on server truth.

title: Change-set engine & merge preview
description: A reviewer can read any proposal's commits, files, and diffs computed server-side against the fork point, trust that collisions are real because the merge was attempted, and preview the landing outcome before committing — no clones, no CLI on the review path.

title: Landing: one click, with receipt
description: A chosen proposal lands server-side in one click; every attempt yields one of nine unambiguous, numbered outcomes; the reviewed-state and concurrency preconditions make 'what lands is what was reviewed' true, and each landing records its validation evidence.

title: Live platform events
description: The platform proves it is alive: pushes, forks, and landings flow through a single-consumer, deduped, validated event pipeline to the UI in real time, with polling existing only as the degraded fallback.

title: Judge layer
description: A reviewer gets three typed advisory signals per proposal — risk, intent-vs-diff, semantic collision — from a server-assembled, pinned, fail-closed judge; chips advise while code decides, and thresholds are calibrated before any gating is trusted.

title: Trust: secrets, intent & provenance
description: Secret-class values never leave the worker — schema-only rendering, scrubbed free-text channels, withheld folds, 409-blocked landings — while every change-set durably carries its why via the notes mirror and its provenance stays visible.

title: Agent workspaces & harness onboarding
description: An operator provisions N isolated agent workspaces from one baseline in one command and onboards real agent CLIs — omp, codex, and BYO harnesses — through a machine-legible standard; each workspace pushes independently and emits events.

title: Identity: auth seam, tokens & elevated reveal
description: The platform is auth-ready and demo-open with zero credential egress: one default-deny authorize() chokepoint, short-lived scoped audited tokens, and elevated reveal existing only behind the seam — enforced before any non-demo data enters.

title: Interactive tour
description: A first-time viewer learns the model in one sitting: a 10-step stepper that teaches with simulations, renders the real proposal set live, quizzes over it, states honest scope, and never breaks.

title: Operational excellence: demo, submission & governance
description: The entry can be reproduced and submitted — committed scripts, rehearsed failure paths, a 5–10 minute uninterrupted take and an open-source package — under the platform's binding operating discipline: pinned runtime, declared scope floor, engineering-law governance.

title: Platform API & client protocol
description: Any client can drive the whole platform through documented, additive-only route shapes that never drift silently; the 11-entity protocol plus push-event surface is the contract the second client later proves.

title: R2 asset tier

title: Enforce server-side exclusive file locks (binary+l semantics)
description:
Per-file atomic first-writer-wins locks enforced server-side (not advisory), with soft and hard modes. A denied open returns lock owner identity; lock state is globally visible and released on submit/revert. This is the central AAA requirement for non-mergeable binaries.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §5 req#1 (L174) + §1 +l/f (L31,43)

title: Store multi-GB binaries natively without LFS pointer rewriting
description:
First-class versioned storage for .uasset/.umap/.pak/.bik/.fbx up to several GB, with no separate pointer tier that rewrites Git object IDs and no plan cap below multi-GB (GitHub LFS caps at 2-5 GB; non-LFS hard-blocks >100 MiB).
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §5 req#2 (L175) + §4 (L149-152)
acceptance_criteria: A 3 GB+ asset commits, versions, and checks out byte-identical on a second client; no per-file cap below multi-GB; history stores deltas not full copies per small edit.

metadata.check_cmd: e2e: commit 3 GB asset; fresh clone checkout byte-identical

title: Build CDC chunk store for game assets in R2
description:
Content-defined chunking (GearHash/Rabin/FastCDC; target 64 KiB-8 MiB) stores content-addressed chunks in R2 so edits invalidate only nearby chunks. This is the core game-asset/R2 tier replacing LFS full-copy-per-revision storage.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §2.1 (L48-66) + §6 Pattern A/F (L175-198) + Open Q1/Q4 (L204-207)
acceptance_criteria: A small edit to a 2 GB asset re-uploads only bounded chunks (target <10%); chunk sizes within the configured band.

metadata.check_cmd: 2 GB asset small edit re-uploads bounded chunks (<10%)

title: Write chunk manifests and Merkle integrity into repo
description:
Manifest maps each blob to its ordered chunk hashes and is versioned with the repo; a Merkle tree gives integrity and partial verification, replacing LFS's fragile sha256+size pointer with no chunk-level integrity.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §1.6 (L41-42) + §2.10 (L104-105) + §6 Pattern F (L195-197)
acceptance_criteria: Blob reconstructed from manifest matches its hash; a tampered chunk fails verification.

metadata.check_cmd: reconstruct from manifest matches hash; tampered chunk rejected

title: Serve blobs via presigned direct-to-R2 transfers
description:
Client upload/download goes direct to R2 via presigned URLs (1s-7d) or multipart sessions, because Workers request bodies cap at 100 MB (5 GB Enterprise) and cannot proxy multi-GB assets. Chunks are immutable, so the path is CDN-friendly.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §4.1-4.2 (L132-142) + §6 Pattern D (L187-189)
acceptance_criteria: A 3 GB upload completes without traversing the Worker body path; range download works via presigned URL.

title: Implement lazy hydrated checkout for huge repos
description:
Metadata-first (blobless) checkout with placeholder working tree, hydrate-on-read via FUSE-style mount, local blob cache, and priority for manifests over binaries; ArtifactFS-compatible (hydration concurrency, 30-min prep timeout, dirty overlay). Full clone of a multi-TB game repo is infeasible.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §2.6-2.9 (L88-103) + §6 Pattern C (L183-185)
acceptance_criteria: Clone of a multi-GB repo completes metadata-only; first read hydrates the file; a cache hit avoids refetch; dirty writes survive in overlay.

metadata.check_cmd: blobless clone + first-read hydration; cache hit avoids refetch

title: Split storage: source in Artifacts, big binaries in R2
description:
Artifacts caps (1 GB/repo, 32 MB/blob) force large files into R2 while Artifacts holds source, pointers, and manifests; enforce the size cutover automatically so repos stay within limits. Each primitive plays to its strength.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §4.4 (L149-152) + §6 Pattern E (L191-193); research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §6 Artifacts limits (L207-208)

title: Build predictive validation so merged SHA equals tested SHA

title: Do binding-side diffing; no clones in review paths
description:

acceptance_criteria: Review requests resolve diffs via binding reads; no clone step exists in the review path and p95 diff latency is under 1s at demo scale.

title: Repo-per-agent + fork-from-baseline isolation
description:
Isolation is solved and commoditized: repo (or worktree) per agent forked from a baseline with one comparison view; reject shared-workspace soft isolation (PaperBench: soft 55.5% below single-agent 57.2%; worktree 63.3%).

acceptance_criteria: Each agent works in its own fork with no shared mutable workspace; the platform presents all forks in one view.

description:

title: Pin isomorphic-git 1.42.x; never disk-checkout untrusted trees

Ref: technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/research.md:56,102

Question sets live in code, versioned with the platform, referenced by setId in every /judge call; responses carry the setId they answered. Prevents per-feature prompt policy drift.

Thresholds and weights live in code and are tuned on our own labeled proposals, never copied from a cookbook; typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. Required before any gate fires on real landings.

(demo SHOULD) Give a proposal a stable identity that survives re-pushes so cards, links, and provenance can reference it beyond a repo+ref pairing.

Every completed unit of work emits a receipt onto the shared artifact (swarm R3); receipts are evidence for the trust bundle and fork-card proof cluster.

title: Classify every file with System-1 models at ingest
description:
Engineering law 2: fast/cheap models classify every file and directory (type, security level, tags) near-instantly so per-file security levels do not require an expensive LLM read.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:14,30; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 3,8
acceptance_criteria: Every file in a change-set carries classification metadata produced by a System-1 pass at ingest.

title: Route expensive reasoning only to files needing judgment
description:
Two-tier intelligence routing: cheap classifiers cover every file while expensive reasoning reads only what needs judgment, feeding review, issue triage, and risk fields.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:30,37; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8 (law 2)
acceptance_criteria: The reasoning layer processes only files flagged by tier-1 classification; unflagged files never reach it.

title: Build semantic index and context maps for repos
description:
Vector/semantic index of the codebase plus context maps so agents and the UI traverse by meaning and see architecture - grep alone is a fail; agents inspect just enough, never total reads.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:15,31,37; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 8.4-8.5
acceptance_criteria: A semantic query returns architecture-relevant results for a repo and a context map orients an agent without total reads.

title: Keep durable work/state tier (queue, presence, leases)
description:
Storage class 2: durable, expiring, frequently-written state - task queue, presence, authoring leases, secret-typed flags, stashes - as the platform's coordination layer.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 3 (class 2); _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:44-46
acceptance_criteria: State survives restarts with TTL semantics; queue and presence are readable through the API.

title: Implement surgical expiring advisory locks
description:
Locks are scope/entity-level, expiring, and advisory-first; never fleet-wide serialization. This backs declare-before-touch and lease semantics without blocking agent fleets.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:36; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 3,8.6
acceptance_criteria: The lock API supports per-entity scope, TTL, and advisory mode; a fleet is never blocked by one lock.

title: Ship tool manifest and structure map into workspaces
description:
Engineering law 3 (self-describing platform): deliver a machine-readable tool manifest plus structure map into every agent workspace so no agent is context-blind about available tools or platform structure.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:13,29; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.3
acceptance_criteria: Every workspace contains the manifest and structure map, and an agent can enumerate tools and structure from them.

title: Enforce denied paths: deny, close, redirect, escalate
description:
Swarm R2 sharpened: a denial is a wall, not an obstacle - count retries on forbidden paths (e.g. bash-grep retried after 'use the grep tool'), close the path, force the sanctioned alternative, and escalate on repeat.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:43,45; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 6 (R2)
acceptance_criteria: Repeated forbidden attempts hit a closed path with a sanctioned-alternative response and an escalation record.

title: Write claims, status, receipts onto the shared artifact
description:
Swarm R1 sharpened: communicate through the work - claims, status, and receipts live on the shared artifact; any agent orients locally with no hub and no global truth.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:44; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 6 (R1)
acceptance_criteria: An agent can join a task correctly by reading artifact claims alone, with no central coordinator.

title: Require declare-before-touch and completion receipts
description:
Swarm R3: collision avoidance with zero global knowledge - declare intent on the artifact before touching the work, write a receipt when finished.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:46; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 6 (R3)
acceptance_criteria: Work without a prior claim is detectable, and completion always emits a receipt.

title: Standardize agent output: summary, detail, affordances
description:
Communication contract: every agent output is summary + structured detail + affordances (clickable next actions that feed back as signals); standardize the interface, not the intelligence (BYO model/harness).
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:40,47; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 6
acceptance_criteria: Outputs validate against the contract and their affordances render and post signals back in the UI.

title: Implement join-don't-restart with merge/refactor
description:
Swarm R4: if someone already claimed or started the work, join instead of restarting; prefer LLM merge/refactor of theirs+ours over regenerating equivalent code, economically and socially.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:49; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 6 (R4)
acceptance_criteria: The flow offers a join path with a merge/regenerate estimate and flags duplicate work instead of silently rebuilding it.

title: Declare intent: router pings before work starts
description:
Intent router: declare what you are about to build and the platform matches it against the fork ecosystem, replying '80% done by fork X' before work begins - automating join-don't-restart as a platform reflex.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:58,74; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 5
acceptance_criteria: Posting an intent returns fork-match pings with candidates before any work starts.

title: Return matcher verdicts: merge, context, or ignore
description:
Three-state verdict for fork comparison: merge it (their work does the job), use as context (partial fit; build with their implementation in hand), or ignore (different goal).
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:64; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 5
acceptance_criteria: The matcher emits one of the three verdicts with rationale for each candidate.

title: Run background matcher against the fork ecosystem
description:
A background sub-agent continuously diffs other forks' work against our PRD/prompt/implementation/goal; when their work fulfills the goal it recommends direct merge or use-as-context, otherwise adapt.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:62; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 5
acceptance_criteria: A live fork gets compared and a verdict surfaces without the user explicitly asking.

title: Render fork cards with six signal clusters
description:
Fork cards carry six signal clusters - fit/overlap, people/trust, liveness, proof, distance, cost-to-adopt - and signals trigger investigation, never auto-decision ('then we investigate'). Concrete card design remains open.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:52-57; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 4,5,10.3
acceptance_criteria: A fork card displays all six clusters and never auto-selects a fork; it prompts investigation.

title: Surface active-fork radar in context
description:
Critical social layer: surface active and relevant forks where the user is working so siloed duplicate work becomes visible; agents can discover other forks' agents.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:23,32; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 5
acceptance_criteria: Relevant active forks appear in context with their activity state.

title: Weave workspaces through the whole experience
description:
Engineering law 12: workspaces are woven through the entire platform experience and merging feels transparent, seamless, and understandable - not a bolt-on.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:11; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.12
acceptance_criteria: Workspace and merge state is present in every relevant surface, not siloed in one page.

title: Enforce scoped, single-use write tokens for landing
description:
Landing mints a repo-scoped write token, uses it once, and revokes it in a finally block; failure paths hand out no write credential (spine AD-9).
Ref: built: platform/src/land.ts; source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-pitch.md section 'Why this is buildable' (scoped tokens)
acceptance_criteria: The token is revoked after both success and failure and no write credential ever leaves the worker.

title: Apply per-path storage policies (compressed/delta/head-only/keep-n)
description:
Configurable revision storage per asset class: full-compressed (+C), RCS delta (+D), head-only (+S), keep-last-n (+Sn), uncompressed (+F), changeable thereafter. Studios tune this per asset class to trade size vs retrieval cost.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 file types (L26-45) + §5 req#3 (L176)
acceptance_criteria: Policy is set per glob/extension, observable in revision count/sizes, and changeable via CLI/API.

metadata.check_cmd: assert depot growth differs per policy on same asset history

title: Auto-classify files by extension with locked-binary defaults
description:
Extension rules auto-assign storage/merge classes and default binary+l for art/level types (.uasset, .umap, .png, .fbx, ...), with type-change operations supported. Mirrors Perforce file-type defaults so artists need no per-file decisions.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 file types (L26-45) + §3 UE integration (L104-107)
acceptance_criteria: New .uasset commits lock-on-edit by default; an edited rule is reflected on next classification.

metadata.check_cmd: e2e: new .uasset path locks on edit by default; rule edit takes effect

title: Provide partial sync via workspace views and sparse streams
description:
Per-user workspace maps only the needed repo subtree; sparse/virtual streams give a read-only parent plus writable subset; per-file selective download so a 500 GB repo never needs 500 GB local. Maps to client-spec/stream and Gluon selective-sync prior art.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §5 req#4 (L177) + §1 workspaces (L16-20) + §4 partial sync (L154-159)
acceptance_criteria: Sparse checkout of a subtree succeeds while unmapped content is absent locally; per-file selective download works.

metadata.check_cmd: sparse checkout materializes subset; unmapped paths absent

title: Support atomic changelist commits and server-side shelves
description:
Multi-file commits succeed or fail as a unit with numeric IDs, and unsubmitted changelists can be shelved server-side for review/test/resume. Shelving is the Perforce primitive feeding pre-commit review.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 changelists (L22-24) + §5 req#5 (L178)
acceptance_criteria: A fault-injected partial commit leaves no partial state; a shelf can be listed, reviewed, and resumed.

metadata.check_cmd: fault-injected partial submit leaves no partial commit; shelf round-trips

title: Review art assets visually: preview, annotate, approve/reject
description:
Thumbnails/previews for 2D/3D/video/audio with annotation and approve/reject workflows; art assets reviewed separately from code but versioned in the same repo (Swarm + DAM model).
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §5 req#7 (L180) + §3 DAM (L96-98)
acceptance_criteria: A .png/.fbx/.wav asset opens a preview with comments and an auditable approval state transition.

metadata.check_cmd: asset preview opens for png/fbx/wav; approve transition auditable

title: Enforce per-file ACLs by path, user, group and IP
description:
Protections down to file/depot-subtree granularity, per user/group/host (IP), with access levels (list/read/open/write/review/admin) and LDAP/SAML/OIDC identity. Contractors can be IP-restricted.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 protections (L55-57) + §5 req#8 (L181)
acceptance_criteria: A user denied on a protected path is allowed elsewhere; evaluated levels per rule; identity from external IdP.

metadata.check_cmd: denied read on protected path; allowed elsewhere; levels enforced

title: Build transaction hooks for policy gating and notifications
description:
Server-side hooks at submit/commit/push transaction points for policy enforcement, CI gating, and notifications, extensible by script or API. Same role as Perforce triggers in front of submissions.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 triggers (L51-53) + §5 req#11 (L184)
acceptance_criteria: A pre-commit hook rejects a submission; a post-commit hook delivers a notification.

metadata.check_cmd: pre-commit hook rejects submission; post-commit notifies

title: Treat binaries as never-merge; keep 3-way text merge
description:
Binary types are flagged to never merge (lock instead) while text gets 3-way merge; the platform detects and prevents binary merge attempts rather than silently last-push-wins. Complements the lock service.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §5 req#12 (L185) + §1 no-merge rationale (L47-49)
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent binary edits cannot be merged; second writer is steered to locking; text merge unaffected.

metadata.check_cmd: concurrent binary edit cannot merge; text merge unaffected

title: Offer artist mode: download, lock, edit, check-in
description:
Gluon-style simplified surface for artists - selective download, lock, edit, check-in - that hides branching and merge concepts entirely. Lowers the barrier for art teams who should never need to understand streams.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §3 UVCS/Gluon (L109-114) + §4 (L154-159)
acceptance_criteria: An artist completes an asset update end-to-end without branch commands; locks enforced throughout.

metadata.check_cmd: artist updates asset without branch commands; lock enforced

title: Deduplicate chunks across files and versions
description:
Chunk reuse across assets and versions with a dedup-check API so clients skip uploading known chunks; three-tier dedup (session, local cache, global). Kills the LFS cost pathology where each push stores a full new copy.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §2.1 Xet (L52-58) + §6 Pattern A (L175-177)
acceptance_criteria: Two copies of the same asset store once; re-upload after a small edit uploads <10% of chunks; dedup check skips known chunks.

metadata.check_cmd: duplicate asset stored once; dedup check skips known chunks

title: Support film-scale blobs via R2 multipart storage
description:
Single assets of 2-8 GB and VFX plate stacks beyond 5 GB, using R2 multipart (4.995 TiB max) and single-part (5 GiB) mechanics so no plan cap blocks real production content.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §1.2-1.3 (L13-31) + §4.1 (L132-135)
acceptance_criteria: A 6 GB blob uploads and downloads intact through the multipart path.

metadata.check_cmd: 6 GB blob upload/download intact via multipart

title: Harden transfers: resumable uploads, 413/429 backoff
description:
Batch-style transfer client with resumable multipart uploads, rate-limit backoff (413 too-large, 429), retries and idempotency for interrupted transfers. Needed to move multi-GB assets over real networks.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §1.5 (L37-39) + §4.4 (L149-152)
acceptance_criteria: An interrupted 4 GB upload resumes without restarting; a throttled client backs off and completes.

metadata.check_cmd: interrupted 4 GB upload resumes; 429 client backs off and completes

title: Federate Windows/GPU/macOS runners via queue bridge
description:
Cloudflare cannot run Windows/GPU/macOS, so external runners register and receive jobs via Queues/webhooks while a Workflow waits for completion (waitForEvent). Requires idempotent dispatch, at-least-once delivery, runner health checks, and cancellation propagation.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §4 cannot-run table (L159-164) + §5 req row 8 (L180) + §6 federation risk (L210-213)
acceptance_criteria: A job dispatched to an external runner returns status; a cancelled job propagates stop to the runner.

metadata.check_cmd: external runner receives job via queue; cancel propagates

title: Define pipelines as code: triggers, matrices, reuse
description:
Declarative pipeline spec with push/PR/schedule/dispatch triggers, event chaining, matrix fan-out, concurrency groups, caching, artifact handling, and nested reusable workflows. Parity baseline is GitHub Actions' 30+ events and 256-cell matrices.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §1 triggers/matrix (L9-32) + §3 Dagger (L94-95)
acceptance_criteria: A spec compiles to a job DAG; a matrix expands and reports per-cell status; a reusable pipeline is invoked from another.

metadata.check_cmd: spec compiles to DAG; matrix cells report individually

title: Run batch merge queues on speculative groups
description:
Batch interdependent proposals against trunk speculatively, validating the combination before any merge, so main never breaks from a set-level interaction. No native merge queue exists; implement batch validation in a Workflow.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §3 merge queues (L118-125) + §5 req row 7 (L179)
acceptance_criteria: Two interdependent proposals validate as a batch and merge together; a conflict in the batch blocks the group.

metadata.check_cmd: two interdependent proposals validate as batch then merge

title: Inject secrets via OIDC with short-lived credentials
description:
Repo/org/environment-scoped secrets plus auto-provisioned scoped automation tokens, with OIDC federation to cloud providers so no long-lived credentials persist; secrets inject into sandbox envs. No native OIDC-to-self-hosted-runner bridge exists - build one.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §1 secrets/OIDC (L24-25) + §6 secrets model (L197-200)
acceptance_criteria: A deploy job authenticates via a short-lived OIDC token; no plaintext secret appears in logs.

metadata.check_cmd: deploy authenticates via OIDC; no plaintext secret in logs

title: Publish preview deployments per proposal branch
description:
Branch push deploys a live preview URL while the production branch deploys to prod, via Workers Builds and Artifacts integration (deploy hooks, 20-min build timeout, 10 GB/project cache, 7-day LRU). Preview environments are the standard review surface.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §2 Workers Builds (L38-52) + §3 preview envs (L127-132)
acceptance_criteria: Opening a proposal yields a live preview URL; merging to production branch deploys the site.

metadata.check_cmd: proposal branch yields live preview URL; prod branch deploys

title: Add branch protection and defined concurrent-push semantics
description:
Artifacts documents no branch protection and leaves concurrent-push semantics undefined; define and enforce protected refs and deterministic concurrent-push handling so races cannot corrupt base refs. Extends the shipped merge/conflict layer.
Ref: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/imports/artifacts-recon-brief.md Critical gaps (L27-32)
acceptance_criteria: A protected ref rejects unauthorized force updates; two concurrent pushes resolve deterministically or are rejected with a clear error.

metadata.check_cmd: protected ref blocks force update; concurrent pushes deterministic

title: Consume Artifacts events over Queues into a live feed
description:
Queue consumer records Artifacts push/fork/create events and exposes the newest 50 via GET /events. The event feed is a hint surface for the UI and automation.
Ref: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/imports/artifacts-recon-brief.md Events (L16); built: platform/src/index.ts:1-3, platform/CONTRACT.md §/events

title: Auto-merge commits that pass all parallel validation gates
description:
A commit that clears cryptographic, performance and regression checks in the parallel pipeline merges to mainline automatically; humans review architectural intent only.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L52 (§3 Automated Mainline Triage); docs/STATE.md queue auto-land-gate-live
acceptance_criteria: A green proposal lands without a human click while a red one is refused with recorded reasons.

title: Speculative validation on predicted edits (demo SHOULD)
description:
The moment a branch or workspace appears, background Workers begin compiling and testing predicted edits so validation is complete by the time the commit lands.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L381 (§2 Speculative CI/CD Testing); L479; demo-scope.md SHOULD map (speculative validation)
acceptance_criteria: Opening a workspace with known in-flight edits produces validation evidence before the commit is pushed.

title: Secret-typed file primitives (cryptographic boundary nodes)
description:
Add polymorphic file primitives to the Git object model: .env, credentials.json and certificates are typed secret objects with file-level access control, not uniform text blobs.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L536-538 (§1 Secret-Typed Object Primitives); L520 (user: per-file auth level); SPEC.md CAP-8
acceptance_criteria: A committed secret-class file is classified as a typed node and access is enforced per file.

title: Schema-only decoupled views for secret files (demo beat)
description:
Clones and openness show only the schema definition of a secret file (for example DATABASE_URL: String); values are decoupled, encrypted with hardware-bound keys and stored in isolated KV.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L539 (§1 The Decoupled View: Zero-Trust Metadata); SPEC.md CAP-8; demo-scope.md story step 6
acceptance_criteria: Opening a repository containing .env shows key names and types, never live values.

title: Commit-time Wasm secret scrub with security isolation branch
description:
A native WebAssembly scanner runs on incoming pushes; raw secrets committed into markdown or documentation are isolated at the edge, scrubbed, and routed to a security isolation branch.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L541 (§1 Automated Leak Scrapers); L589 (Edge-Scrubbing Wasm Hooks); L520 (user: scrape context docs); demo-scope.md story step 6
acceptance_criteria: A seeded leak commit is scrubbed before propagation and the isolated copy plus evidence are recorded.

title: Decision log appended to commit metadata
description:
Every agentic modification appends an immutable decision log (autonomous choices that never reach commit messages) directly into commit metadata.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L551 (§2 Decision Logs & Trace Archaeology); L601 (Trace Archaeology Ledger); L520 (Whiteboard summary)
acceptance_criteria: A commit exposes its decision log through notes/metadata without external systems.

title: Approvability score and check-run auto-approval of low-risk PRs
description:
Codebase-aware review computes a plain-English Approvability score and auto-approves low-risk pull requests through check-run agents.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L50 (Macroscope)
acceptance_criteria: A low-risk proposal auto-approves while a risky one is held with reasons.

title: Per-line AI attribution surviving rebase, squash and cherry-pick
description:
Link individual lines to the exact AI agent session, model and prompt that generated them, and keep that attribution metadata intact through rebases, squashes, merges and cherry-picks.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L58 (Git AI)
acceptance_criteria: After a rebase or squash, a line's attribution still resolves to the original agent session and prompt.

title: Structural conflict detection: entity/AST-level, not just textual
description:
CAP-3 calls for structural as well as textual conflict classification; current kinds are textual. Add entity/symbol-level overlap detection (same function/class touched by two proposals).
Ref: SPEC.md CAP-3 success (structural vs textual); platform/src/index.ts conflict kinds
acceptance_criteria: Two edits to different functions of one file classify mergeable, while edits to the same function classify structural conflict.

title: Elevated reveal for authorized viewers (demo beat)
description:
The CAP-8 demo beat includes an elevated reveal; today values can never be revealed. Design an authorized, auditable reveal path (role or token plus audit trail) without weakening default masking.
Ref: SPEC.md CAP-8 success; platform/CONTRACT.md masking law
acceptance_criteria: An authorized viewer can reveal a value and the reveal is audited; an unauthorized request is denied.

title: Commit-time scrub of secrets leaked into non-secret paths
description:
Masking is path-driven by design, so a secret committed into a normal file passes through. Add commit-time leak detection/scrub (pattern/entropy scan) and show the scrub in the demo beat.
Ref: SPEC.md CAP-8 success (commit-time scrub); platform/CONTRACT.md Secret classes note
acceptance_criteria: A commit adding an obvious credential in a normal source file is flagged and scrubbed at commit time.

title: Per-worker secret API (H5)
description:
Interface contract H5: a per-worker secrets API so agents get scoped secret access through the platform rather than the filesystem surface.
Ref: interface-contract.md What Agent Office lacks (H5)
acceptance_criteria: A worker can list and read only its scoped secrets via API; access is audited.

title: Client adapter parity: platform API replaces GitHub as the client store
description:
CAP-9: an external client renders workspace/proposal state from the API alone; the office 11-entity protocol maps onto platform entities so a client adapter can drop-in replace GitHub as the backing store.
Ref: SPEC.md CAP-9; interface-contract.md Feasibility
acceptance_criteria: An adapter pointed at the platform API renders floors/workers/proposals with no GitHub calls.

title: GitHub-semantics synthesis: reviewDecision / mergeStateStatus / mergeable
description:
The client protocol needs GitHub-specific semantics synthesized from platform state so the adapter needs no GitHub; define derived values for the three fields.
Ref: interface-contract.md Feasibility (semantics to synthesize)
acceptance_criteria: Proposal payloads expose the three derived fields with documented, deterministic values.

title: Law 4: repo answers for itself - index, preview, demos, provenance
description:
Semantic index + live preview + native demos + push provenance so comprehension needs no clone; push provenance is partially covered by the event feed.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 4; SPEC.md Constraints (review path never clones)
acceptance_criteria: From the repo page a user can read the semantic index, preview the app and trace push provenance without cloning.

title: Law 5: agents inspect just enough - context maps over total reads
description:
Context maps plus semantic index orient an agent without total reads; expose the orientation surface to agent harnesses.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 5
acceptance_criteria: An agent can answer what/where/why for a repo from context maps instead of reading every file.

title: Law 7: contribution standard as a service (platform-side lint/conventions)
description:
Platform-level contribution standards (lint, conventions, changelogs, commit rules) enforced platform-side with no per-repo scaffolding.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 7
acceptance_criteria: A pushed change-set is checked against platform contribution standards with findings shown on the card.

title: Law 9: work-item to change-set linkage on one review surface
description:
Work items and change-sets reference each other so review stays on one surface; ties into Task/Issue entities and proposal cards.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 9
acceptance_criteria: A proposal card shows its linked work item and a work item shows its change-sets.

title: Law 12: merge/workspace transparency woven through the experience
description:
Merging feels transparent, seamless and understandable rather than a bolt-on; preview-merge and one-click land are early pieces, workspace lifecycle weaving is not yet built.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 12; platform/ui/app.js:664-775
acceptance_criteria: A user can follow join, compare, merge and provenance as one continuous flow with no dead ends.

title: Swarm R1: communicate through the work (claims/receipts on the artifact)
description:
Simple standardized communication: claims, status and receipts are written onto the shared artifact so any agent orients locally with no hub and no global truth.
Ref: engineering-laws.md swarm R1
acceptance_criteria: An agent can read another agent's claim/receipt from the shared artifact and orient without a central registry.

title: Swarm R4: join-don't-restart as a platform reflex
description:
Prefer reusing existing work (LLM merge/refactor) over regenerating equivalent code - socially and economically; the intent router is the mechanism, this is the reflex.
Ref: engineering-laws.md swarm R4; fork-community.md
acceptance_criteria: When near-duplicate work exists, the platform surfaces the reuse path before generation starts.

title: Communication contract: summary + structured detail + affordances
description:
Every agent output is summary plus structured detail plus affordances (clickable next actions feeding back as signals); outputs are control surfaces, not dead reports.
Ref: engineering-laws.md Communication contract
acceptance_criteria: Agent outputs render as actionable controls whose actions feed back into the platform as signals.

title: Tier 1: codebase vector index + semantic traversal
description:
Codebase vector index serving semantic traversal rather than grep, so agents and reviewers reach relevant code without total reads.
Ref: stack.md Storage classes tier 1; engineering-laws.md law 5
acceptance_criteria: A semantic query returns relevant files/symbols for a natural-language intent.

title: Entity API: Floor / Project (repo, branch, cloning, counts)
description:
Client-readable floors/projects with id, name, repo, branch, cloning and worker counts (workers/busy/waiting).
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Floor / Project)
acceptance_criteria: GET /floors returns the fields; counts track live workers.

title: Entity API: Worker (provider/model/effort, desk, status, worktree, pr, usage)
description:
Worker entity exposing provider/model/effort, desk, status, worktree {branch,path,base}, pr, task, activity and usage.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Worker)
acceptance_criteria: GET /workers returns the fields for each live worker.

title: Entity API: Task / Queue (issue, title, prompt, status, outcome, pr)
description:
Task/queue entity exposing provider/model/effort, issue, title, prompt, status, workerId, branch, outcome and pr.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Task / Queue)
acceptance_criteria: GET /tasks returns queued and running tasks with the fields above.

title: Entity API: Issue (number, title, state, labels, assignees, body)
description:
Issue entity with number, title, state, author, labels, assignees, taken flag and body.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Issue)
acceptance_criteria: GET /issues returns issues in the client-readable shape.

title: Entity API: Presence / Peer (position, voice, sharing, doing, floor)
description:
Presence entity with id, name, position, voice, sharing, doing and floor.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Presence / Peer)
acceptance_criteria: GET /presence returns current occupants for a floor.

title: Entity API: Settings (limits, leave-on-merge, agent, prompts, theme)
description:
Settings entity exposing limits, leave-on-merge, default agent, prompts and map/theme preferences.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Settings)
acceptance_criteria: GET/PUT /settings round-trips platform settings.

title: Events: worker lifecycle + worktree (spawn/update/remove, worktree)
description:
worker.spawn/update/remove and worker.worktree events emitted on the normalized bus.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: Spawning or updating a worker emits the matching event.

title: Events: terminal streaming (term.data/snapshot/input) + screen
description:
Terminal streaming protocol with snapshot plus per-row diffs plus scrollback plus input, and screen events for worker views.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events and API needs (terminal streaming protocol)
acceptance_criteria: A client receives a terminal snapshot, incremental row diffs and can send input.

title: Events: floor lifecycle (enter/added/removed)
description:
floor.enter/added/removed events on the normalized bus.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: Floor membership changes emit events.

title: Events: issue/pull lifecycle (gh.* platform-native equivalents)
description:
Issue and pull lifecycle events as platform-native equivalents of the gh.* events clients consume today.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: Proposal open/update/land emits lifecycle events consumable by a GitHub-shaped adapter.

title: Events: queue state
description:
Queue state events so clients see task queue movement live.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: Task enqueue/dequeue emits queue state events.

title: Events: peer presence (join/update/leave/move/act/emote)
description:
peer.join/update/leave/move/act/emote events for the presence surface.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: Peer presence changes emit the matching events.

title: Provider-agnostic agent launch: unify 8 harness formats
description:
Client architecture needs provider-agnostic agent launch that unifies the eight harness formats behind one platform contract.
Ref: interface-contract.md API needs (provider-agnostic agent launch)
acceptance_criteria: Two different harnesses can be launched through one platform API shape.

title: Cost attribution + budget enforcement
description:
Attribute cost per worker/task and enforce budgets, as required by the client architecture.
Ref: interface-contract.md API needs (cost attribution + budget enforcement)
acceptance_criteria: A worker exceeding its budget is stopped or flagged, with cost visible per task.

title: Landing policy engine: branch protection and merge policy
description:
Artifacts has no server-side merge/diff/conflict/branch-protection, so the platform builds policy: protected branches, required evidence, landing rules.
Ref: stack.md What the platform builds (policy); SPEC.md Constraints (no branch protection)
acceptance_criteria: A protected baseline refuses a landing that lacks required evidence or policy checks.

title: Intent router: declare intent first, match before building
description:
Declare intent first; the platform matches it against the fork ecosystem and pings '80% done by fork X' before work begins.
Ref: fork-community.md The intent router; SPEC.md CAP-10
acceptance_criteria: A declared intent triggers a pre-work match result naming candidate forks.

title: Fork-card six-cluster signals (fit, trust, liveness, proof, distance, cost)
description:
Fork cards carry six signal clusters (fit/overlap, people/trust, liveness, proof, distance, cost-to-adopt vs regenerate) that trigger investigation, never auto-decision. Concrete card design is still undecided.
Ref: fork-community.md Fork-card signals; fork-community.md Deferred (card design)
acceptance_criteria: A fork card renders the six clusters with per-cluster signals.

title: Score landing-subset risk for proposal combinations
description:
Score how safe landing a chosen combination (A+B vs A+C) is, so reviewers can compare subsets before committing. Consumes collision and duplication answers where present.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:47 (#7)
acceptance_criteria: For any subset of two or more pending proposals, /judge returns a subset risk score with per-level probabilities and the landing UI can compare two subsets.

metadata.check_cmd: POST /judge { setId: 'subset-v1', target } returns a score with level probabilities

title: Detect duplicated behavior across proposals and forks
description:
A noul across proposals and forks asking whether the behavior is already covered elsewhere. Drives a merge-it-instead recommendation instead of landing a duplicate.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:48 (#8)
acceptance_criteria: A proposal re-implementing behavior from another proposal or fork is flagged duplicate with the overlapping source identified.

metadata.check_cmd: Seed two proposals implementing the same behavior in different files; the later one is flagged duplicate

title: Detect stale proposals against moved bases
description:
A noul asking whether a proposal is obsolete because the base moved or another proposal landed the same behavior. Keeps the pending set honest as the base advances.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:49 (#9)
acceptance_criteria: A proposal whose behavior already landed on base is flagged stale; one still applicable is not.

metadata.check_cmd: Land a change on base, then re-judge the overlapping proposal; stale flag set

title: Verify post-merge behavior against expectations
description:
A verify question comparing expected versus observed behavior after landing, using test output or screenshots as evidence. Surfaces a regression signal when the observed result contradicts the intent.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:50 (#10)
acceptance_criteria: The post-land judge records a supports / contradicts / insufficient verdict with an evidence reference; contradicts marks the landing for review.

metadata.check_cmd: Land a proposal with a failing post-merge test; verdict = contradicts in the landing record

title: Sniff new dependencies and CI edits for supply-chain risk
description:
Choice benign / suspicious / malicious over new dependencies, obfuscated blobs, network calls, and CI edits. Routes suspicious changes to a security queue and blocks on high confidence.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:56 (#13)
acceptance_criteria: A proposal adding an obfuscated blob or unexplained CI edit is classified suspicious or worse and enters the security queue; high-confidence malicious blocks landing.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge a fixture diff adding a postinstall script with a network fetch; classified suspicious or worse

title: Screen public contributions before human triage
description:
Nouls for author-change mismatch, task-scope violation, and spam signals, triaging public PRs before a human sees them.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:57 (#14)
acceptance_criteria: A public contribution outside the declared task scope is flagged pre-triage with the signal named.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the public-PR fixture; scope-violation flag set before human review

title: Scan intent and notes text for secrets and PII leaks
description:
A noul asking whether the provenance text itself (intent, notes) leaks secrets or PII before publication. Complements the AD-4 free-text scrub by judging semantic leakage the regex scrub misses.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:58 (#15)
acceptance_criteria: An intent containing a paraphrased credential is flagged before the provenance is published; a clean intent is not.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge a fixture intent containing a paraphrased key; leak noul > tuned threshold

title: Flag breaking changes with semver signal
description:
A noul plus major/minor/patch choice over the diff. Feeds release gating and changelog semantics.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:62 (#16)
acceptance_criteria: A diff removing or altering a public API surface is flagged breaking with a semver suggestion.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the breaking-API fixture; breaking=true + major

title: Escalate proposals whose diffs exceed stated scope
description:
Nouls for touches_auth / public_api / billing / schema / ci; escalate when the diff exceeds the stated task. Keeps narrowly-scoped agents from silently widening blast radius.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:63 (#17)
acceptance_criteria: A proposal whose diff touches an undeclared sensitive area is escalated with the touched areas listed.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge a fixture diff editing auth while the intent says docs-only; escalate

title: Estimate review effort to order the human queue
description:
Score skim / focused / deep so the human queue sorts by risk times effort. Reduces reviewer overload in the set view.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:64 (#18)
acceptance_criteria: Every card shows an effort level and the queue can be sorted by risk times effort.

metadata.check_cmd: curl /proposals | jq '.[0].judge.effort'

title: Route proposals to reviewers by expertise match
description:
Choice over reviewer profiles and expertise to route each proposal to a specialist. Consumes the platform's reviewer roster.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:65 (#19)
acceptance_criteria: A judged proposal returns a suggested reviewer drawn from configured profiles; with no profiles configured it returns no suggestion, never a fabricated one.

metadata.check_cmd: Configure two profiles, judge a schema-touching proposal; the schema profile is chosen

title: Gate behavior changes without matching tests
description:
A noul asking whether a behavior change lacks a matching test. Surfaces the gap on the card and to policy before landing.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:66 (#20)
acceptance_criteria: A behavior-changing diff with no test delta is flagged test-insufficient.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the no-test fixture; test_sufficient=false

title: Flag public API changes missing docs updates
description:
A noul asking whether a public API change lacks a docs update. Surfaces doc debt before merge.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:67 (#21)
acceptance_criteria: A public-API change without a docs diff is flagged docs-incomplete.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the public-API fixture with no docs edit; docs_complete=false

title: Check new dependencies against the stated task
description:
A noul asking whether a newly added dependency was actually needed for the stated task. Catches dependency bloat and unnecessary supply-chain surface.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:69 (#23)
acceptance_criteria: A new dependency unrelated to the intent is flagged dependency-unnecessary.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge a fixture adding a date library to a docs-only change; flag set

title: Suggest reviewable splits for mega-proposals
description:
Score per hunk whether changes are independent, then suggest reviewable splits for mega-proposals. Keeps large agent outputs reviewable in the set view.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:73 (#24)
acceptance_criteria: A multi-behavior proposal yields a split suggestion grouping independent hunks; the suggestion never changes content, only review groups.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the seeded mega-proposal fixture; at least one split suggested with hunk groups

title: Triage issues by type, priority, and component
description:
Choice bug/feature/question plus priority score plus component choice for the issues module. Automates first-pass triage.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:74 (#25)
acceptance_criteria: A new issue receives type, priority, and component, and the issues module renders them.

metadata.check_cmd: POST /judge set issue-v1 with an issue body; typed answers returned

title: Classify landed commits for changelog generation
description:
Choice breaking/feat/fix/perf per landed commit so release notes render from code templates. Never asks the model for prose.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:75 (#26)
acceptance_criteria: Each landed commit carries one classification and the changelog generator emits grouped release notes from templates.

metadata.check_cmd: Land the demo set, then generate a changelog draft grouped by classification

title: Triage CI failures and recommend retry policy
description:
Choice flake/infra/real/timeout plus a retry-safe noul to drive retry policy. Avoids blind retries of real failures and manual triage of flakes.

acceptance_criteria: A flaky test signature is classified flake with retry-safe=true; a real failure is classified real with retry-safe=false.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge two CI log fixtures; expected classes plus retry flags

title: Evaluate release-readiness checklist with nouls
description:
Nouls per release checklist item, aggregated in code into a readiness verdict. Advisory on the release surface.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:77 (#28)
acceptance_criteria: A release missing checklist items shows a readiness verdict listing the unmet items; all-met yields ready.

metadata.check_cmd: Run the release-readiness set against the demo repo; unmet items enumerated

title: Check active claims before agents start tasks
description:
A noul run before an agent starts: does an active claim already cover this task? Enforces swarm rule R4 (join, don't restart).

acceptance_criteria: Starting a task under an active overlapping claim warns or rejects and points to the claim; a non-overlapping task proceeds.

title: Review UI diffs visually from before/after screenshots
description:
Feed before/after screenshots (Clef's multimodal encoder, up to 4 images) with nouls for visual regression, layout breakage, and unreadable text. Extends review to rendered output.

acceptance_criteria: A visually broken after-screenshot raises layout-broken; an unchanged pair raises no regression.

title: Check changes against design tokens and palette
description:
Score whether the change matches design tokens, palette, and spacing. Advisory chip for UI-touching proposals.

acceptance_criteria: A deviating palette or spacing change scores below the tuned threshold and is flagged.

title: Sign agent identities for proposals
description:
Signed identity per agent/author so the trust bundle and fork-card people/trust cluster can rely on verifiable provenance instead of reputation alone.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:57; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 4; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-pitch.md section 'What it does' (signed identity)
