title: Persist provenance/artifact tier (traces, previews)
description:
Storage class 3: git-notes, per-worker traces, receipts, live previews, screenshots/videos, and demo links - the artifacts that let the repo answer for itself without cloning.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 3 (class 3); _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:17,31
acceptance_criteria: Provenance records are retrievable per proposal and per worker; preview artifacts are addressable.

title: Make stashing simple and safe
description:
Stashing must not be difficult or feel losable; expose a platform-level stash with durable state instead of a fragile local-only mechanism.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:18; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 3
acceptance_criteria: A stash survives session loss and is restorable from the UI or API.

title: Enable interactive output pages with action buttons
description:
An agent can emit a live web page whose buttons spur the conversation forward; outputs become control surfaces, not dead reports, sharing the review UI's whitespace.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:41,48
acceptance_criteria: An agent-produced page renders with working actions that post signals back into the conversation.

title: Monitor and block sandbox-escape attempts
description:
Agents must respect the boundaries of their box: the platform detects and records sandbox-escape attempts and enforces the boundary rather than trusting the agent.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:42
acceptance_criteria: An escape attempt is detected, recorded, and surfaced or escalated while the boundary holds.

title: Support BYO models and harnesses via launch abstraction
description:
Provider-agnostic agent launch so teams bring their own model and harness; at minimum the platform standardizes agent output, plus MCP-style worker management tools.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:40,87; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 7
acceptance_criteria: Agents from at least two providers or harnesses are launched through one interface and expose uniform management.

title: Show unique fork-vs-fork diffs
description:
See a fork's unique diff versus yours so overlap and divergence are obvious before deciding to join or merge back.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:23,32
acceptance_criteria: A fork comparison renders a unique-diff view against the user's base.

title: Enable agent-to-agent cross-fork conversations
description:
Agents discover and talk to other forks' agents to coordinate work and reduce duplicate effort (collaboration initiation as a platform primitive).
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:23,32
acceptance_criteria: Agents on different forks exchange messages or claims through the platform.

title: Facilitate merge-back to upstream
description:
Drive more merge-back to upstream so fork work stops being siloed; upstream contribution from a fork becomes a supported flow with provenance.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:23
acceptance_criteria: Fork changes can be proposed and merged back upstream with their provenance intact.

title: Score fork people/trust signals
description:
Fork cards carry trusted-developer signals: personal plus community reputation; diverse signals that trigger investigation rather than a single opaque score.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:53,57
acceptance_criteria: A fork card shows signer and reputation evidence for its contributors.

title: Collect liveness and automation evidence signals
description:
Liveness cluster: velocity, recency, self-gardening; CI/CD presence and auto-fix harnesses count as liveness and quality evidence on a fork card.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:55,57
acceptance_criteria: A fork card shows velocity/recency plus automation evidence when present.

title: Cluster feature types and tag commits via System-1
description:
System-1 clustering of feature types with commits carrying tags; an alignment test flags when planned work matches a tag aligned with another fork's work, prompting investigation.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:54
acceptance_criteria: Commits receive feature-type tags and alignment detection suggests fork investigation.

title: Resolve and implement partial-fit handling policy
description:
Open question: the operational policy for the 'otherwise' branch when a fork's work only partly fulfills the goal. The verdict 'use as context' exists; the policy for acting on it does not.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:63; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 5,10.1
acceptance_criteria: A documented partial-fit policy exists and the router/matcher behavior follows it.

title: Auto-tag and classify issues with fast models
description:
Fast-model structured auto-tagging/classification for issues with better differentiation than label free-for-alls; the idea is captured but not specced.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:24; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 10.8
acceptance_criteria: New issues receive structured tags/classification from a fast model.

title: Model milestones and epics as first-class timeline objects
description:
Milestones and epics speak project-management language as first-class, checkout-able timeline objects - version navigation in project language, not convoluted tags.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:12,28; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.10
acceptance_criteria: An epic/milestone object links to changes and can be checked out from the timeline.

title: Make historical version checkout painless
description:
Viewing and checking out old versions is currently painful; provide version navigation over the timeline so old states are easy to inspect and restore.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:12
acceptance_criteria: A user can check out an old version in no more than two actions from the UI.

title: Link work items and change-sets bidirectionally
description:
Engineering law 9: work items and change-sets reference each other so review stays on one surface, feeding both PM integration and the canvas.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:35; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.9
acceptance_criteria: A proposal shows its work items and a work item shows its change-sets.

title: Serve contribution standards platform-side
description:
Engineering law 7: Husky-style contribution standards as a service - deterministic and non-deterministic rules enforced platform-side with no per-repo scaffolding; agents adhere immediately.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:19,33; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.7
acceptance_criteria: Rules configured once at platform level apply to all repos and agents.

title: Auto-generate changelogs as a platform feature
description:
(demo COULD) Platform-level auto-changelogs (git-cliff, semantic-release, release-drafter, conventional-changelog, changesets) for optimal speed and accuracy without per-repo tooling.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:20; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:92 (COULD); _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.7
acceptance_criteria: A changelog is generated from repo history by the platform itself.

title: Lint commits as a platform feature
description:
Platform-side commit linting with no per-repo config; agents adhere immediately to the platform standard.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:20; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.7
acceptance_criteria: A non-conforming commit is flagged or rejected by the platform rule.

title: Unify README and file-view repo navigation
description:
Repo navigation is disjointed between README and file view; provide one coherent browsing surface over documentation and files.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:21
acceptance_criteria: One navigation surface covers readme, files, and releases without context switches.

title: Improve releases and tags navigation
description:
Releases and tags navigation is poor; make release objects browsable and navigable in project language.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:21
acceptance_criteria: The releases/tags view supports navigation and inspection of release objects.

title: Reach GitLens-class parity, contextually woven
description:
(demo COULD) GitLens feature parity at platform level while fixing its UI failure: features are woven contextually, discoverable in place, never buried in hundreds of tabs.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:22,34; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:92 (COULD); _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.8
acceptance_criteria: A parity feature list is implemented with in-place discovery.

title: Build one continuous surface, no tab explosion
description:
See cross-page information at a glance without leaving the page: SPA-like continuity, glanceable overlays, and work-item-to-change-set links instead of tab hops.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:27,35; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.8
acceptance_criteria: Key cross-page information appears in place with no forced tab hopping.

title: Answer for the repo without cloning
description:
Engineering law 4: semantic index + live preview + native demos + push provenance deliver comprehension without cloning; previews, screenshots, videos, and demo links are built in, not bolted on.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:17,31; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.4
acceptance_criteria: A repo overview surfaces preview/demo artifacts and provenance before any clone.

title: Track push provenance (laptop vs production)
description:
See the bigger ecosystem: per-commit push origin provenance (laptop versus production) as part of the trust and artifact surface.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:16
acceptance_criteria: A commit carries origin provenance surfaced in the UI.

title: Expose worktree-as-a-service API
description:
From Agent Office's needs: worktree-as-a-service - the platform provisions and tears down per-worker worktrees server-side.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:87
acceptance_criteria: An API call provisions an isolated worktree for a worker.

title: Normalize worker events across provider hook formats
description:
Unify the eight provider hook formats into one normalized worker-event bus with push delivery, replacing Agent Office's 90s polling assumption.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:87 (unify 8 provider hook formats); _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:89
acceptance_criteria: Events from at least two providers normalize into one schema on the bus.

title: Stream terminals: snapshot, row diffs, scrollback
description:
Terminal streaming protocol: snapshot plus per-row diffs, scrollback, and input, mirroring the headless-xterm model Agent Office already uses.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:86,87
acceptance_criteria: A live terminal stream renders with working input round-trip.

title: Attribute worker cost and enforce budgets
description:
Cost attribution and budget enforcement per worker, supporting always-on fleets and the platform's System-1 economics.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:87; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 7
acceptance_criteria: Cost per worker is visible and an over-budget worker is constrained.

title: Publish global presence roster API
description:
Gap H7: a global presence roster (who and what is active where) as an API entity for clients and coordination.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:90 H7; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:81
acceptance_criteria: The presence roster lists active workers and their locations (floors/workspaces).

title: Expose per-worker secrets API
description:
Gap H5: a secrets API per worker so secret-class values reach workers through a controlled channel and never enter change-sets or diffs.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:90 H5
acceptance_criteria: A worker resolves a secret handle without its value appearing in any change-set.

title: Capture per-worker trace provenance
description:
Gap H4: per-worker trace provenance - the session trail behind a change-set, feeding the trust bundle's proof cluster.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:90 H4
acceptance_criteria: A proposal links to the worker trace that produced it.

title: Support host git or native proposal model
description:
Gap H2: remove the local-git assumption - the platform hosts git or provides a native proposal model so clients like Agent Office do not need a local repo.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:90 H2
acceptance_criteria: The proposal flow works without any client-local git.

title: Expose 3D-renderable entities: floors, workers, queues
description:
The API must expose 3D-renderable entities and events - floors, workers, queues, boards, presence - so spatial clients can render the platform.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:81; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 7
acceptance_criteria: The entity and event API covers all five named kinds.

title: Wire remaining Cloudflare substrate (DO, Workflows, R2)
description:
Artifacts, Workers, Queues, KV, and assets are in use; extend to Durable Objects (coordination), Workflows (orchestration), and R2 (blobs) as the product grows beyond the demo.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-pitch.md section 'Why this is buildable'; current bindings in platform/wrangler.jsonc
acceptance_criteria: Each remaining substrate binding is used by at least one real feature.

metadata.check_cmd: platform/wrangler.jsonc (current bindings: artifacts, queues, kv, assets)

title: Measure System-1 cost/accuracy vs expensive reads
description:
Open question 10: the confidence-model claim that System-1 classification beats expensive-LLM reads on per-file security levels is asserted, not measured; validate the economic moat premise with numbers.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:97; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 10.10
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark numbers compare System-1 versus expensive reads on classification and security levels.

title: Replicate content to regional edges with central write authority
description:
Regional edge/proxy servers serve file content locally while the commit server keeps central write authority, with delta-sync sending only changed bytes per revision. Needed for multi-continent studios.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §2 topology (L63-68) + §5 req#6 (L179)
acceptance_criteria: A remote-region client receives deltas and cached content; writes still sequence through central authority.

metadata.check_cmd: remote region fetch receives delta bytes only; central write preserved

title: Hit big-repo performance envelope (10k tx/min, 10+TB)
description:
Target sub-100 ms metadata operations, thousands of concurrent users, 10,000+ transactions/minute, 10+ TB repos and petabyte total data without sync/submit degradation; delta transfers for large files. These are Perforce's published capacity figures to match.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §2 capacity (L70-75) + §5 req#9 (L182)
acceptance_criteria: A load test on a synthetic 10 TB repo sustains transaction and latency targets.

metadata.check_cmd: load report vs targets on synthetic 10TB repo

title: Ship lock-aware Unreal/Unity/Godot editor plugins
description:
Editor plugins show lock status, prevent silent overwrites, and auto-lock on asset edit (UE already flags .uasset binary+l). Lock awareness must move into the tools artists actually use.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §3 UE integration (L104-107) + §5 req#10 (L183)
acceptance_criteria: Editing a locked .uasset in UE is blocked with owner shown; save auto-locks the asset.

metadata.check_cmd: UE/Unity plugin blocks edit of locked asset; auto-lock on save

title: Model policy-driven stream branches with derived views
description:
Branching model with metadata (mainline -> release -> development): workspace views auto-derive from the stream spec, merges flow down then up, and sparse/virtual streams restrict the view. A branch-with-policy concept beyond plain Git refs.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §1 stream depots (L11-14)
acceptance_criteria: A stream created with policy auto-generates matching views; merge direction rules are enforced.

metadata.check_cmd: stream created with policy; view auto-derived; direction enforced

title: Add asset metadata, tagging and search (DAM features)
description:
Custom metadata, AI-assisted tagging, high-res thumbnails and USD-native previews for art assets, with browse/search across the repo. The DAM layer on top of versioning that studios use to find assets.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §3 Helix DAM (L96-98)
acceptance_criteria: An asset is found via tag/metadata query; thumbnail renders; metadata edits persist.

metadata.check_cmd: search by tag returns asset; thumbnail rendered

title: Import Git/LFS/Perforce/SVN with transitional sync
description:
Migration importers for existing histories (including binary assets) with bi-directional sync during transition so teams can move incrementally. Competitors advertise automated migration; it is table stakes for displaced Perforce studios.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §3 Diversion migration (L116-121) + §3 SVN (L127-129)
acceptance_criteria: Import of a test repo preserves history; transitional sync keeps both sides consistent.

metadata.check_cmd: imported repo preserves history; bi-directional sync converges

title: Add binary delta encoding for archive-like assets
description:
Optional VCDIFF-style delta encoding (xdelta3/RFC 3284) where chunking alone is insufficient, storing per-revision deltas for near-incompressible archives and executables.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §2.2 (L68-77)
acceptance_criteria: A 1-byte change to an archive yields a bounded delta; patch reconstructs the file byte-identically.

metadata.check_cmd: 1-byte change to archive yields bounded delta; patch byte-identical

title: Invalidate edge caches on mutable ref updates
description:
Immutable chunks cache forever, but mutable refs (branch heads, latest pointers) must invalidate and propagate consistently at the edge; define the cache-invalidation contract for pointer objects.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §4.1-4.2 (L132-142) + §6 Pattern D + Open Q6 (L209)
acceptance_criteria: After a push, a fresh clone sees the new head immediately with no stale-ref window.

metadata.check_cmd: push then fresh clone sees new head; no stale ref served

title: Add content-addressed registry for build outputs
description:
Immutable build artifacts stored in R2 keyed by content hash while source and lockfiles stay in the repo (Nix-style); outputs dedupe across builds and cache forever. Completes the source-vs-package boundary.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §3.2-3.3 (L117-126) + §6 Pattern G (L199-201)
acceptance_criteria: Two builds with identical inputs produce the same key and the second download is a cache hit.

metadata.check_cmd: second build hits content-addressed cache

title: Harden CI supply chain: pinning, egress control, scoped creds
description:
Dependency locking, egress firewall for build jobs, and ephemeral least-privilege credentials to blunt tj-actions-style exfiltration attacks. GitHub is only adding these natively in its 2026 roadmap, so shipping them is differentiation.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §1 pain points supply chain (L31)
acceptance_criteria: A build attempting unexpected egress is blocked; dependency versions are pinned and verifiable.

metadata.check_cmd: unexpected egress blocked; dependency versions pinned

title: Add poisoning-resistant remote build cache
description:
Task-graph remote cache with authenticated per-repo/tenant writes (70-85% hit rates achievable) that defends against CREEP-style cache poisoning (CVE-2025-36852), where PR actors could poison production bucket caches.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §2 Workers Builds caching (L52) + §3 Nx/Turborepo CREEP (L112)
acceptance_criteria: A cache hit skips rebuild; an unauthorized cache write is rejected.

metadata.check_cmd: unauthorized cache write rejected; hit skips rebuild

title: Autoscale warm runner pools to kill cold starts
description:
Elastic runner fleet with warm pools and burst autoscaling targeting sub-30 s job starts, versus GitHub's 30-60 s provisioning and manual concurrency groups. Off-peak scheduling can absorb non-latency-sensitive bursts.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §1 pain points queue/cold start (L27-29) + research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §4 scheduling (L113)
acceptance_criteria: A 100-job burst starts within target; warm-pool metrics are observable.

metadata.check_cmd: 100-job burst starts within target; warm pool metrics

title: Select affected tests with AST-aware analysis
description:
Incremental test selection driven by static/AST analysis of the change, cutting fan-out cost on monorepos. Candidate tooling (testless-class) runs inside a sandbox; no native AST service exists.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §5 req row 3 (L174)
acceptance_criteria: Tests for unchanged modules are skipped; a change to a module triggers its dependent tests.

metadata.check_cmd: unchanged module tests skipped; changed module tests run

title: Ensure hermetic, reproducible builds with pinned images
description:
Hermetic build definitions with pinned container images and locked inputs so the same pipeline runs identically in dev and CI. No native Nix/Bazel exists on the stack; container images must be pinned manually.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §5 req row 5 hermetic (L176) + §3 Dagger/Nix (L95,116)
acceptance_criteria: Identical inputs reproduce byte-identical outputs twice; image digests are pinned.

metadata.check_cmd: same inputs reproduce byte-identical outputs; images pinned

title: Engineer around Artifacts size and rate limits
description:
Platform-scale fan-out must respect 1 GB/repo, 32 MB/file, 1 TB/account (raiseable), 2k control-plane requests/10 s per namespace and 2k git requests/10 s per repo via sharding, caching, and backoff.
Ref: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/imports/artifacts-recon-brief.md Limits (L22-25)
acceptance_criteria: Sustained load stays under limits through sharding/backoff; no 429 storms under fan-out.

metadata.check_cmd: sustained fan-out under 2k req/10s limits with sharding/backoff

title: Add observability for repo and agent event streams
description:
Per-tenant metrics and event analytics (GraphQL dataset artifactsEventsAdaptiveGroups plus platform metrics) covering pushes, clones, locks, pipelines, and agent activity.
Ref: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/imports/artifacts-recon-brief.md Observability (L18)
acceptance_criteria: A dashboard shows repo event rates and pipeline durations per tenant.

metadata.check_cmd: dashboard shows repo event rates per tenant

title: Attach editors: devcontainers, VS Code Remote, web IDE
description:
devcontainer.json-compatible workspace definitions so local editors attach over SSH/Remote, plus an optional hosted code-server/Theia proxied by a Worker. Latency budget: <100 ms for interactive editing; agent turns tolerate 1-5 s.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §1 devcontainers (L20) + §3 remote-dev (L77-82) + §6 interop (L212-217)
acceptance_criteria: Local VS Code attaches to a cloud workspace via devcontainer; the hosted web IDE loads and edits a file.

metadata.check_cmd: local VS Code attaches to cloud workspace; web IDE optional

title: Manage workspace sizing, snapshots and capacity
description:
Instance types lite (1/16 vCPU, 256 MiB) through standard-4 (4 vCPU, 12 GiB, 20 GiB disk), account ceilings (6 TiB memory, 1,500 vCPU, 30 TB disk), snapshots (20 GB, 30-day TTL), and scheduling policies (default/durable_object/off-peak).
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §4 Containers row (L113)
acceptance_criteria: Resize and snapshot-restore are verified; account-limit alarms fire before ceilings.

metadata.check_cmd: resize + snapshot restore verified; account ceilings alarmed

title: Fork stateful sandboxes for parallel what-ifs
description:
Pause/fork a running workspace (microVM snapshot) to explore multiple paths from identical state; persistence outlives a single session. Targets ~90 ms creation and sub-200 ms restore where the platform allows.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §2 patterns 5-6 + Daytona row (L44,52-53)
acceptance_criteria: A forked sandbox continues independently from the same state without affecting the source.

metadata.check_cmd: forked sandbox diverges independently from same state

title: Support multi-repo workspaces for agent reasoning
description:
Mount/checkout multiple repositories in one workspace so an agent reasons and edits across repos, with per-repo credentials and correct remotes for cross-repo commits.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §2 pattern 7 (L54)
acceptance_criteria: Two repos are mounted; a cross-repo change commits with correct remotes.

metadata.check_cmd: two repos mounted; cross-repo commit remotes correct

title: Add agent computer-use verification artifacts
description:
Agents drive the built app in a browser (computer-use) and capture screenshots/video/log artifacts attached to the proposal for review. Cursor-style verification loop as a platform capability.

title: Offer Dynamic Workers tier for short jobs
description:
JS/Python/WASM snippets run in Dynamic Workers as a cheap isolated alternative to containers for short tasks, with documented capability boundaries.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §4 Sandbox row Dynamic Workers (L114)
acceptance_criteria: A short job runs isolated in a Dynamic Worker at lower cost than the container path.

title: Document boundaries and federation story for judges
description:
Honest capability matrix: CF runs orchestration, web-native CI, and Linux sandboxes; GPU/Windows/macOS/console devkits federate to external runners. Avoid overclaiming; show the hybrid architecture explicitly in the submission.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §4 absence matrix (L121-138) + research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §4 (L159-164)
acceptance_criteria: Submission includes the CAN/CANNOT matrix plus a federation diagram and limitation statement.

title: Prove Workers + Artifacts compliance for judges
description:
Competition rules require Workers and Artifacts as a minimum (additional primitives allowed); keep the usage demonstrable and record the $25k credits prize and Oct 14 2026 deadline in the submission checklist.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/bigassets-recon-brief.md §5 competition terms (L165-169)
acceptance_criteria: Submission artifacts run on Workers + Artifacts; compliance checklist is signed with evidence links.

title: Adopt task-dependent fan-out; do not chase max agents
description:
The agent optimum is task-dependent (four agents on Commit0, two on PaperBench): expose concurrency as a tunable with guidance rather than a race to maximum agents.
Ref: technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/research.md:48
acceptance_criteria: Demo declares per-task agent count with rationale; UI discourages unbounded fan-out.

title: Ship a pre-write conflict-check hook for agents
description:
clash-style hook so agents are stopped before writing into a known collision instead of discovering it at merge time.
Ref: competitive-multi-agent-git-platform-landscape-2026-10-02/research.md:96-104; agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/verify-round-1-trajectory.md:53
acceptance_criteria: An agent write into a contested path is blocked or warned pre-write with the conflicting change named.

title: Design review for acceptance, not raw detection
description:
Published mining shows rejections are dominated by invalid, redundant, or out-of-scope suggestions: optimize suggestions for cheap evaluation (acceptance engineering).
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:51,53
acceptance_criteria: Review output is a triage-ordered, deduplicated suggestion list with per-item evaluation cost estimated.

title: Run execution-backed review in sandboxes
description:
Close the loop from 'suggests' to 'proves' (live probes against previews; tests written and run in a sandbox; autofix iterating until tests pass): offer execution results as review evidence.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:47
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can attach an execution result (test run or probe) to a proposal verdict.

title: Match review-UX table stakes per proposal
description:
Match CodeRabbit/Greptile-class reviewer UX (summary, inline comments, one-click fixes, learnings, guideline files) so the set-level product is not weaker per change than single-change reviewers.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:53,161
acceptance_criteria: Per-proposal view offers a summary, inline comments, and a one-click fix path.

title: Add flaky quarantine and bisect-on-failure
description:
After a batch failure, auto-bisect to the offending change and quarantine known flaky tests/agents instead of blocking the queue.
Ref: competitive-multi-agent-git-platform-landscape-2026-10-02/research.md:80; agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:162
acceptance_criteria: A failing batch bisects to the culprit; a quarantined flake no longer blocks subsequent landings.

title: Echo stacked-diffs/patch-series landing workflow
description:
Proven human-scale discipline (Meta ~100% adoption; Google chained CLs): support dependent stacks with per-change identity and defined submission order.
Ref: technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/research.md:51,40
acceptance_criteria: A stack of dependent changes lands in order; mid-stack updates rebase dependents without losing identity.

title: Scope replication per agent with predicate shapes
description:
ElectricSQL predicate shapes and Jazz row-level permissions: replicate only permitted files/rows to each agent's view.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:109,170
acceptance_criteria: An agent's view omits files outside its grant; revocation removes them live.

title: MCP server exposing set context to external agents
description:
MCP grew 10k -> 18k+ servers and is LF/AAIF-hosted; provide an MCP surface so external agents can query the change map, conflict graph, and verdicts.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:93,168
acceptance_criteria: An external MCP client can list sets and fetch a proposal's diff/provenance via tool calls.

title: Sign landed commits and set attestations keylessly
description:
Add gitsign/sigstore-style keyless signing of landed commits and set verdicts so provenance is verifiable, not just recorded (SLSA: provenance does nothing unless inspected).
Ref: competitive-multi-agent-git-platform-landscape-2026-10-02/research.md:102; agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:141
acceptance_criteria: A landed commit signature verifies against the platform's identity issuer.

title: Add AI-restricted repository mode
description:
The Codeberg/Sourcehut segment is real: an explicit per-repo mode that refuses agent-authored changes (and LLM training use) as a first-class trust feature.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:85,89,166
acceptance_criteria: A repo in AI-restricted mode rejects agent-originated pushes while accepting human ones.

title: Add code-linked diagrams with click-through to source
description:
Whiteboard precedent: agent-drawn diagrams/annotations pinned to code line ranges, clickable through to source, beat text-only diffs for comprehension.
Ref: competitive-multi-agent-git-platform-landscape-2026-10-02/research.md:108; agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:169
acceptance_criteria: A pinned annotation navigates to the exact source line in the review view.

title: Surface decision logs per change (human vs agent)
description:
A decision log separates human and agent decisions per change, giving a reviewable history of why the set looks as it does.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:169
acceptance_criteria: Each change shows an ordered decision log with actor type and timestamp.

title: Add cognitive-debt reduction: fold tests and boilerplate
description:
Fold test/boilerplate noise in review so humans see behavioral change; 2026 analytics show duplication +81% and refactoring -70%, so reviewers must not pay for churn.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:147,384
acceptance_criteria: Triage view can fold declared test/boilerplate hunks while keeping behavioral hunks visible.

title: Show cost-per-review transparency
description:
The review/sandbox market's most confused axis: surface active-work-based cost per review/verdict in the UI rather than hiding it in credits.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:131,384
acceptance_criteria: Each review shows its model/tool cost; an aggregate cost-per-verdict is displayed per set.

title: Add copy-for-agent handoff from triage
description:
Whiteboard's 'Copy for Agent' handoff: a reviewer decision/hunk can be handed back to an agent as a structured task rather than prose in chat.
Ref: competitive-multi-agent-git-platform-landscape-2026-10-02/research.md:108
acceptance_criteria: Reviewer copies a decision; an agent receives a structured instruction referencing the change/hunk.

title: Budget for Artifacts billing start 2026-10-14
description:
Artifacts billing begins 2026-10-14 (10k ops/mo free, then $0.15/1k ops + $0.50/GB-month): the demo must fit the free tier or carry an explicit budget.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:119,365
acceptance_criteria: Estimated ops/storage for the demo path is documented against the free tier.

title: Instrument and export engineering-analytics metrics
description:
The analytics market pivoted to proving AI impact (cycle time, revert rate, review lag; review/validation is the binding constraint): instrument queue/review latency and throughput, attribute them per agent, and export DX/LinearB-compatible metrics.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:151,384
acceptance_criteria: Metrics export includes cycle time, revert rate, review lag, and agent attribution; a dashboard shows review latency and landing throughput per set.

A successful land shows a banner naming the proposal and the resulting commit sha, and the /events ticker reflects the push in near-real-time — the visible proof that the ship happened server-side.
