title: Store platform state as Git repos (profiles, metadata, issues)
description:
Make every user profile, repository metadata set, and issue tracker its own Git repository of JSON/Markdown files so platform state is forkable, diffable and auditable instead of living in SQL rows.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L19-25 (§1 The Core Paradigm: Everything is Git)
acceptance_criteria: A profile or issue change appears as a commit in its own repo and can be forked and merged like code.

title: Bind identity to SSH/GPG keypairs with signed profile repos
description:
Identity is a cryptographic keypair, not a password or centralized OAuth: a user profile is a Git repo signed by that key.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L23-25 (§1 Cryptographic Identity)
acceptance_criteria: An account can be verified from its key alone; commits to a profile that lack a valid signature are rejected.

title: CRDT-backed concurrent review and comment merging
description:
Store parallel reviews and simultaneous comments as CRDTs inside the Git tree so multiple humans or agents can comment offline with no centralized locking and merge seamlessly.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L41 (§2 Radical Parallelization)
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent offline comments on the same line both survive a merge without a manual conflict.

title: DAG-scheduled CI: run independent build tasks concurrently
description:
Model CI/CD as a directed acyclic graph that executes every independent task concurrently across a serverless grid instead of a linear pipeline.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L40 (§2 DAG-Based CI/CD Execution)
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline with parallel branches shows concurrent execution and joins only on declared dependencies.

title: Self-healing agents: analyse, patch, test and open PRs
description:
Autonomous agents continuously run static analysis, write patches for dependency and security flaws, test them, and open PRs unattended.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L50 (§3 Self-Healing Codebases)
acceptance_criteria: A seeded dependency vulnerability yields an autonomous PR with passing validation evidence.

title: Native Git-hook WebAssembly micro-runners at pack arrival
description:
Trigger Wasm micro-runners from server-side Git hooks the instant a push arrives, instead of waiting for a central server to parse a webhook and schedule CI.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L51 (§3 Event-Driven Webhooks via Git Hooks)
acceptance_criteria: A push executes a registered Wasm hook inside the ingestion path and its result is recorded as an event.

title: Immutable content-addressable ledger of platform actions
description:
Append every platform decision (why a runner failed, why a PR auto-merged) to an immutable, publicly verifiable log.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L70 (§5 Content-Addressable Platform Logs)
acceptance_criteria: A merge decision is traceable to a ledger entry that can be independently verified.

title: Logic-aware AST diffs: moves and renames shown as moves
description:
Diffs map how logic changed at AST level: a renamed or moved function renders as one visual move rather than a deletion plus an insertion; Tree-sitter parsing gives grammar-aware changes.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L60 (§4 AST Diffs); is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L74 (Difftastic)
acceptance_criteria: Moving a function between files renders as a single move operation in the diff view.

title: Interactive dependency-graph impact view per commit
description:
Render how a single commit impacts internal architecture and external microservices as an interactive dependency graph.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L61 (§4 Dependency Web GL Graphs)
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a commit highlights the affected modules and services in the graph.

title: Infinite spatial canvas for code, issues, diagrams and logs
description:
Files, issue cards, architecture designs and live logs can be placed anywhere on an infinite spatial plane so tools group contextually around the code being changed.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L155 (§4 Infinite Spatial Canvases)
acceptance_criteria: A user arranges heterogeneous artifacts on one canvas and their positions persist.

title: Semantic zoom: continuous macro-to-micro through containers
description:
Zooming all the way out shows a microservice as a single node; zooming in smoothly reveals packages, then files, then inner functions and code text.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L190-200 (§1 Semantic Zooming)
acceptance_criteria: One continuous zoom gesture traverses service, file and function levels without opening tabs.

title: Collapsible modules: expand inline or shrink to capsules
description:
Any code block or subdirectory collapses into a small high-level capsule or expands its contents inline on the canvas without opening a new tab.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L202 (§1 Collapsible Modularity)
acceptance_criteria: Collapse and expand preserve canvas layout and surrounding context.

title: Contextual clustering: trace affected code from an issue card
description:
Pull an issue card onto the canvas, run Trace Affected Code, and physical elastic lines connect the issue to the code node and its test counterpart.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L206-228 (§2 Multi-Document Orchestration)
acceptance_criteria: Tracing an issue draws links to the affected code and test files.

title: Layered feature planes: branches as floating canvas layers
description:
Main is the base layout; checking out a feature branch creates a semi-transparent floating layer, and modified cards lift up or highlight on that layer.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L232-236 (§3 Layered Feature Planes)
acceptance_criteria: Switching branch planes shows lifted modified cards floating over the base layer.

title: Diff topography: merge ripples and conflict intersections
description:
Pulling changes from main ripples through the bottom layer, showing exactly where top-layer modifications intersect or conflict with the base code.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L237 (§3 Visualizing the Diff Topography)
acceptance_criteria: A main update visibly marks the intersecting cards on the feature plane.

title: Git+AST graph database feeds the canvas layout engine
description:
A localised high-speed graph database indexes Git history and the AST and continuously feeds node data (dependencies, file paths, parent-child structures) into the canvas layout engine.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L247 (§4 The Git-as-a-Graph DB Interface)
acceptance_criteria: Canvas layout queries return dependency and parent-child edges for any repository node.

title: Zero-cold-start Wasm CI fan-out across edge Workers
description:
Split compiling, linting and regression tests into granular fragments fanned across thousands of concurrent Workers with no container cold start.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L380 (§2 Zero-Cold-Start Wasm Runners); L478
acceptance_criteria: A large test suite completes through edge fan-out with per-fragment results joined.

title: Run artefacts as commit sub-trees (logs, telemetry, crashes)
description:
Append build logs, system telemetry and crash reports as sub-trees to the commit that caused them, unifying platform health with code history.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L382 (§2 Immutable Platform Logs); L480
acceptance_criteria: A failed run's logs are reachable from its originating commit without an external CI service.

title: Git-native agent passports with cryptographically signed actions
description:
Every human and AI agent has an unforgeable private-key passport embedded in the Git engine; every action, refactor or patch is a signed commit preserving an audit trail.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L396 (§4 Git-Native Agent Identification); L494 (§4 Git-Native Cryptographic Passports)
acceptance_criteria: An agent action without a valid signature is rejected and every accepted action resolves to its signer.

title: Durable Objects as localised graph coordinates and consensus
description:
Use Durable Objects as hyper-local coordinate systems for graph clusters so regional clusters self-heal and resolve their own consensus without a global database query.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L374 (§1 No Central Control Plane); L457-459 (Cloudflare Edge Foundation)
acceptance_criteria: A region resolves its cluster state with no global round trip.

title: Edge prompt caching for agent context and AST blueprints
description:
Cache static AST graph representations and structural context files in regional KV so millions of agent polls hit a pre-computed semantic cache, cutting latency and token cost.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L669 (§2 Prompt Caching Economics); L697 (Edge Context Optimization Caching)
acceptance_criteria: Repeated context reads hit the cache and measurably lower latency and token spend.

title: AST-granular delta pipeline: test only impacted nodes
description:
Use Tree-sitter to isolate the exact microscopic AST change and trigger only the validation modules for directly impacted downstream nodes instead of a full monolithic pipeline.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L668 (§2 AST-Granular Delta Pipelines); L691 (Incremental AST Testing Pipelines)
acceptance_criteria: Editing one function runs only its impacted dependent test modules.

title: Contextual MFA elevation to reveal or inject secret values
description:
Revealing or injecting a secret node requires a runtime-evaluated cryptographic challenge: WebAuthn/passkey from a human or ephemeral mTLS from an authorised deployment runner.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L540 (§1 Contextual Multi-Factor Elevation)
acceptance_criteria: Secret access is denied without the second factor and granted with it, with the grant recorded.

title: Inline streaming leak deflectors on every canvas and doc write
description:
At 10M-entity scale, every code execution, visual node change and document adjustment passes through an inline edge-native Wasm scanner; a pasted credential is scrambled and isolated before it propagates.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L677 (§3 WebAssembly-Powered Leak Deflectors)
acceptance_criteria: Pasting a credential into a card or log description is scrambled and flagged instead of stored.

title: Tree-sitter AST graph as the repository read model
description:
Parse every commit with a native Rust/Tree-sitter engine into an AST; agents read structural node relations (Function X modifies Class Y) instead of raw strings and text greps.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L549 (§2 Native AST-Graph Architecture); L520 (user: stop grepping everything)
acceptance_criteria: Querying a symbol returns its structural relations without any text-grep path.

title: Machine-readable repo context capsule (Repomix engine)
description:
Every repository segment compiles its tree, dependency map and API interfaces into a dense deterministic JSON/Markdown context index so agents ingest a blueprint in milliseconds instead of raw source.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L550 (§2 The Markdown Context Layer Capsule); L593 (AST Context Maps); L675; is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L76 (Repomix / Gitingest)
acceptance_criteria: An agent answers structural questions about a repository from its context capsule alone.

title: Trace archaeology: blame a line back to the agent session
description:
Trace blame links a highlighted line to the exact conversation transcript, prompt and reasoning that produced it, for humans and other agents.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L551 (§2 Decision Logs & Trace Archaeology); L599; L520 (Whiteboard summary)
acceptance_criteria: Given a line of code, the platform returns the originating session, prompt and decision reasoning.

title: Click-to-code interactive diagrams for agent change review
description:
Agents emit structured interactive diagrams (sequence flows, flowcharts, call-stack diffs, database lenses) where clicking any step or box navigates to the exact function and line of code.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L575 (§3 Interactive Click-to-Code Diagrams); L520 (Whiteboard summary)
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a diagram step navigates to its exact code location.

title: Cognitive-debt filters: fold noise, summarise boilerplate
description:
The review surface compresses boilerplate, hides repetitive configuration updates and folds tests and docs away, isolating core architectural logic into readable pseudocode summaries.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L576 (§3 Cognitive Debt Reduction Filters); L520 (Whiteboard AST semantic diff)
acceptance_criteria: A noisy change renders compact with only core logic expanded.

title: Two-way linked canvas nodes and immutable commit hashes
description:
Every node on the visual flow maps directly to an immutable verifiable Git commit hash and back, so visual claims are always traceable to code.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L595-597 (Two-Way Code-Linked Canvas)
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a canvas node resolves to its commit; a commit resolves to its node.

title: Local-first MCP privacy: no telemetry or hosted traces
description:
Model interactions run through secure Model Context Protocol tunnels (local or worker-sandboxed); telemetry and hosted trace capture default off so private code memories never leak to external servers.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L577 (§3 Local-First Privacy with Global Edge Sync); L520 (Whiteboard privacy caveats)
acceptance_criteria: Running agent sessions produces no external telemetry and traces stay local unless explicitly exported.

title: Agent-first plain-file conventions for config and context
description:
Adopt the Vercel-style agent framework principle: agent configuration, skills and context are plain files in the repository that any agent can traverse, version and diff.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L520 (user: Vercel agent framework which is just files)
acceptance_criteria: An agent bootstraps its role and context from repository files alone, with no hidden database config.

title: Plain-English review rules with BYOK and self-hosting
description:
Review configuration is written in natural language, supports bring-your-own-key models and plugins, and can be self-hosted so teams control their review data.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L15 (Kodus)
acceptance_criteria: A natural-language rule blocks a violating change in a self-hosted run with an org-supplied key.

title: Community-governed self-hosted AI PR review agent
description:
The AI PR review workflow runs on the team's own infrastructure using their own LLM tokens, under community governance rather than a hosted vendor.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L16 (PR-Agent by Qodo)
acceptance_criteria: A PR receives an AI review in a self-hosted deployment using locally configured tokens.

title: Rules-driven PR automation and review engine
description:
A rules engine automates pull-request routing, checks and lifecycle actions for engineering teams.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L17 (Reviewpad)
acceptance_criteria: A matching PR is automatically routed and annotated per its rule.

title: Repo-wide semantic review beyond the active diff
description:
Index the whole repository like a vector database so review catches breaking changes, architectural drift and logical flaws in files that were not modified in the pull request.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L48 (Greptile)
acceptance_criteria: A cross-file break introduced by a change is flagged with the affected distant file named.

title: Branchless smartlog: manipulate commits directly in the DAG
description:
Bring Mercurial-style smartlog and branchless workflows to large monorepos: manipulate individual commits in the DAG without manually creating local branch pointers.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L66 (Git-branchless)
acceptance_criteria: A smartlog view shows the commit DAG and supports amend/reorder without branch creation.

title: Chained incremental PR stacking engine with auto-restack
description:
Manage incremental chained pull requests natively across GitHub and GitLab, restacking descendants automatically when a base change updates.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L68 (Git-gud gg)
acceptance_criteria: Updating a base PR restacks its dependent chained PRs automatically.

title: Stacked-branch sync and ship automation
description:
Automate branch synchronisation, shipping and stacked change workflows with a CLI that keeps a stack in sync with its base.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L24 (Git Town)
acceptance_criteria: One command syncs a stack and reports per-branch state.

title: Merge queue with atomic batch validation and stacking
description:
A merge queue groups chained branches, tests each batch atomically and lands only batches that pass, natively supporting stacked PR flows.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L82 (Trunk)
acceptance_criteria: A failing batch is ejected whole while a green batch lands.

title: Batch merge bot: temp branch, full CI, push only if green
description:
Implement the Not Rocket Science rule: a bot builds a temporary branch containing a batch of approved changes, runs the full CI suite against that exact batch and pushes to main only if everything passes.
Ref: is-there-an-open-source-CodeRabbit-or-Graphite.md L84 (Bors-NG)
acceptance_criteria: A daemon lands a batch only after the batch itself passes the full suite.

title: Law 8: ambient capability + GitLens-class parity (demo COULD)
description:
GitLens-class parity surfaced in context - discoverable in place, never buried in tabs, SPA-like continuity with no tab explosion.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 8; demo-scope.md COULD (GitLens-class parity)
acceptance_criteria: GitLens-class features (blame, history, comparison) appear contextually inside the canvas without new tabs.

title: Law 10: PM inspection via milestones as timeline objects (demo COULD)
description:
Milestones/epics are first-class, checkout-able timeline objects in project language, not convoluted tags; PM integration (demo COULD) is the external half.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 10; demo-scope.md COULD (PM integration)
acceptance_criteria: A milestone can be checked out as a workspace baseline and appears as a timeline object.

title: Law 11: always-on System-1 decision layer primed for agents and CI/CD
description:
Cheap System-1 decision agents run continuously, prime the LLM agents doing code work and can drive CI/CD directly; affordability comes from the decision layer being cheap.
Ref: engineering-laws.md law 11
acceptance_criteria: Decision agents run on a schedule, publish signals consumed by code agents, and can trigger pipeline actions.

title: Swarm R2: denial is a wall - count, close, force alternative, escalate
description:
Forbidden paths are a wall, not an obstacle: counted, closed, the sanctioned alternative forced, escalation after N attempts.
Ref: engineering-laws.md swarm R2
acceptance_criteria: A denied path attempt is counted, the alternative is surfaced, and escalation fires after N attempts.

title: Entity API: Whiteboard (strokes + cursors per floor)
description:
Whiteboard entity exposing strokes and cursors per floor.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Whiteboard)
acceptance_criteria: GET /whiteboards returns stroke/cursor state per floor.

title: Entity API: Services (worker, branch, page title, local port)
description:
Services entity exposing worker, branch, page title and local port for running previews.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Services)
acceptance_criteria: GET /services lists a worker's live services with their ports.

title: Entity API: Chat / Notifications (from, text, at)
description:
Chat/notification entity with from, text and at timestamp.
Ref: interface-contract.md Entities (Chat / Notifications)
acceptance_criteria: GET /chat returns recent messages per floor.

title: Events: chat + toast
description:
chat and toast events on the normalized bus.
Ref: interface-contract.md Events
acceptance_criteria: A chat message or toast emits its event.

title: Active-fork radar: in-context relevant forks + unique diff
description:
Surface active, relevant forks in context, show their unique diff versus ours, enable fork-off-fork collaboration and more merge-back to upstream.
Ref: fork-community.md Mechanisms (active-fork radar)
acceptance_criteria: A relevant active fork appears in context with its unique diff vs the current work.

title: Background comparison sub-agent: continuous fork-vs-goal diff
description:
A background sub-agent continuously diffs another fork's work against our PRD/prompt/implementation/goal and returns the verdict shape.
Ref: fork-community.md Mechanisms (background comparison sub-agent)
acceptance_criteria: A running comparison produces refreshed verdicts without a human initiating each comparison.

title: Partial-fit policy: use-as-context branch mechanics (deferred)
description:
The operational policy for partial fits (how the use-as-context branch works mechanically) is explicitly deferred to build and needs trenches time.
Ref: fork-community.md Deferred (partial-fit operational policy); SPEC.md Open Questions
acceptance_criteria: A documented policy exists and the use-as-context verdict carries concrete next actions.

title: Auto-changelog generation (demo COULD)
description:
Auto-changelog from landed change-sets and their intent records; a demo COULD item.
Ref: demo-scope.md COULD (auto-changelog)
acceptance_criteria: Landing a proposal appends a changelog entry derived from its intent.

title: Pod/container visualization (demo COULD)
description:
Visualize worker pods/containers on the canvas; a demo COULD item.
Ref: demo-scope.md COULD (pod/container visualization)
acceptance_criteria: Workers render as visually distinct containers/pods tied to their status.

title: Classify commit messages as conventional, vague, or misleading
description:
Choice conventional / vague / misleading over the commit message paired with the diff. Flag-only signal for review-quality metrics.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:68 (#22)
acceptance_criteria: A message contradicting its diff is classified misleading; a conventional-commit message is classified conventional.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge two fixture messages; expected classes returned

title: Rank candidate forks against a declared intent
description:
Listwise ranking of candidate forks against a declared intent (measured recall@1 0.94 listwise vs 0.87 per-candidate at 1/30th the calls). Powers the someone-already-did-this radar.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:82 (#30)
acceptance_criteria: Given an intent and two or more candidate forks, the top-ranked fork contains the described capability and ranking runs listwise in one call.

metadata.check_cmd: Rank the labeled fork fixture set; recall@1 matches the measured 0.94 baseline

title: Classify game assets by type and lock/preview needs
description:
Choice texture/audio/model/level/video plus nouls for exclusive-lock and preview needs. Roadmap track for the game-asset storage story.
Ref: docs/judge-layer-ideas.md:91 (#36)
acceptance_criteria: A preview asset is classified with needs-preview=true and a large binary gets exclusive-lock=true per policy.

metadata.check_cmd: Judge the asset fixture set; types and lock/preview flags match policy

title: Support fork-off-fork collaboration
description:
Fork-off-fork cooperation as a first-class primitive, not just fork-versus-upstream: sibling forks can coordinate and share work.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:23,32
acceptance_criteria: A fork can declare lineage and coordinate with a sibling fork.

title: Estimate cost-to-adopt vs regenerate for forks
description:
Sixth signal cluster: an LLM-merge estimate comparing adopting a fork versus regenerating equivalent work - economics applied to join-don't-restart.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:57 cluster 6; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 4
acceptance_criteria: The fork card or router shows an adoption-versus-regenerate estimate.

title: Integrate Linear-class PM via common API
description:
(demo COULD) Integrate PM tools rather than imitating GitHub's half-baked milestones/labels: a common API for Linear-class systems, or flesh out projects fully.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:26,35; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.10
acceptance_criteria: At least one PM integration syncs work items with the platform.

title: Expose CI/CD interaction visibility
description:
Show CI/CD interactions in the platform surface so users see automation acting on their change-sets; noted explicitly low priority.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:25; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 10.7
acceptance_criteria: Run status and CI actions are visible per change-set.

title: Visualize containers/pods and running apps if authorized
description:
(demo COULD) Container/pod visualization and running-app visibility when the viewer is authorized, connecting the repo to its runtime.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:16; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:92 (COULD)
acceptance_criteria: Authorized users can see running-app and pod state in the platform.

title: Synthesize reviewDecision/mergeState for clients
description:
Gap H1: Agent Office is tightly coupled to GitHub fields; synthesize reviewDecision and mergeState from platform state so a client adapter can be a drop-in.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:90 H1; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:89
acceptance_criteria: A client receives compatible review and merge-state fields from the platform.

title: Match 11-entity contract; offer GitHub drop-in adapter
description:
Mirror Agent Office's 11-entity contract (Floor, Worker, Task/Queue, Issue, Pull, PR-detail, Presence, Whiteboard, Services, Settings, Chat) so a platform adapter can replace GitHub as the sole backing store.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:89,98; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 7
acceptance_criteria: An adapter maps client calls onto the platform API for all 11 entities.

title: Build toward Agent Office as flagship 3D client
description:
(demo WON'T) Platform stays a web-first product plus API (the heart); Agent Office is the flagship 3D client (the face) to build toward - 3D worlds render platform entities; it is not the core UI and not demo scope.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:75; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md sections 7,2 (WON'T)
acceptance_criteria: The client adapter renders live platform state in a spatial view.

title: Run always-on System-1 decision agents
description:
Rung-2 echo: cheap decision agents run continuously, priming the LLM agents that do code work; context-swapping between background subagents is constant and affordable because the decision layer is cheap.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:67,68,71; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 8.11
acceptance_criteria: A decision agent runs on a cadence and feeds a work agent end-to-end.

title: Let decision agents drive CI/CD directly
description:
Non-LLM decision frameworks feed and prime LLM agents and can directly drive CI/CD workflows when the decision is mechanical.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:68
acceptance_criteria: A System-1 decision triggers a CI/CD workflow without human or LLM mediation.

title: Prototype rung-2 echoes: agent memory, routing
description:
Design for the echoes already visible at rungs 1-2: agents holding memory and compute between themselves and intelligent routing of even basic work - not the mind-uploading nebula.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:77,84
acceptance_criteria: Agent memory persists across sessions and routing decides work placement.

title: Design account-level macro-merging
description:
Long arc: mass-level mergers of company portfolios and their software - 'companies as a service', account-level ecosystem merging rather than individual applications.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:79
acceptance_criteria: A design covers merging two accounts' software ecosystems with provenance.

title: Write competitive differentiation positioning
description:
Open question 9: assert the convergence layer plus social layer as the differentiator with head-to-head positioning, grounded in the research that no shipping product does set-level proposal triage.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 10.9; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-pitch.md section 'What the research says'
acceptance_criteria: A positioning document exists and is grounded in the research matrix.

title: Instrument fork-reuse decisions for merge policy
description:
Fork-reuse and merge preferences cannot be fully decided in advance - they need trenches time; capture operational data so the policy can be derived later.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/.memlog.md:50; _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-intent.md section 10.2
acceptance_criteria: Join/reuse decisions are logged and reviewable as data for deriving policy.

title: Implement binary asset locking (exclusive-open)
description:
Git LFS has no locking while Perforce's exclusive-open model is the proven pattern for binary assets; bring asset lock semantics to the platform alongside the text merge model.
Ref: source: _bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-next-git-platform-2026-10-02/brainstorm-pitch.md section 'What the research says' (Git LFS no locking; Perforce exclusive-open)
acceptance_criteria: A binary path can be exclusively locked and checkout is blocked while the lock is held.

title: Position in market with seatless storage-based pricing
description:
Respond to the March 2026 Unity VCS shift (unlimited seats, 25 GB free storage, usage-based overage) and Perforce cloud at $39/user/month; define our free tier and storage/egress metering model. Pricing is a competitive weapon for large studios.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/perforce-recon-brief.md §6 pricing (L189-216)
acceptance_criteria: Pricing spec published with free tier, storage metering, and no per-seat charges.

metadata.check_cmd: pricing spec published with free tier + storage metering

title: Evaluate WASI-based hermetic CI steps
description:
Spike WASI 1.0 capability-based isolation for hermetic CI steps (no network unless granted). Experimental: no production CI system uses Wasm natively yet, so this is a research track.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/cicd-recon-brief.md §3 Wasm-based CI (L134-135)
acceptance_criteria: A spike runs a WASI step with network denied by default and reports feasibility.

metadata.check_cmd: WASI step denies network by default (spike)

title: Support us/eu jurisdictional data residency
description:
Jurisdiction (us/eu) is immutable at namespace creation; relevant for EU studios and regulated content. Data-localization guarantees must be surfaced in provisioning.
Ref: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/imports/artifacts-recon-brief.md Jurisdictions (L17)
acceptance_criteria: A namespace created in eu keeps its data in the EU region.

metadata.check_cmd: eu namespace keeps data in EU jurisdiction

title: Queue changes offline and sync on reconnect
description:
Graceful degradation when disconnected: local-first clone with periodic sync, agent work queued until reconnect, and optional CRDT (Automerge/Yjs) for edit-then-merge. Online-first is acceptable for v1; offline is a stated open question.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §6 offline (L183-187)
acceptance_criteria: Changes made offline sync on reconnect without loss or duplication.

metadata.check_cmd: offline edits sync on reconnect without loss

title: Mitigate single-product sunset risk via composability
description:
Firebase Studio/Project IDX sunsets Mar 2027 after Google disabled signups - a cautionary precedent; emphasize that Workers + Artifacts + Sandbox are substitutable layers, not a single-product bet.
Ref: research/2026-10-02-platform-recon-briefs/clouddev-recon-brief.md §5 caution (L159-161)
acceptance_criteria: Architecture doc names each substitutable layer and the fallback path.

metadata.check_cmd: architecture doc names substitutable layers

title: Interop: act as a layer above GitHub/GitLab
description:
Treat incumbents as integration targets: import/export changes, read AGENTS.md, and target alongside GitHub/GitLab rather than replacing hosting; GitHub is the best integration target.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:89,166
acceptance_criteria: A repo mirrored from GitHub can be triaged on the platform and a landed change exported back.

title: Evaluate structured merge (tree-sitter/GumTree) beyond line merge
description:
Line-based merge is structurally inadequate at agent churn (41.7% cross-agent textual conflicts, ~42% structural): Mergiraf's tree-sitter+GumTree structured merge and grammar-aware diffs are borrowable future tiers; tree-sitter at the edge is viable but unmeasured.
Ref: technical-next-gen-git-platform-on-cloudflare-2026-10-02/research.md:49,57,91; agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:164,168
acceptance_criteria: Written evaluation compares entity merge vs structured merge on a seeded multi-agent corpus; edge CPU numbers recorded if the spike runs.

metadata.check_cmd: Spike report with cold-start/CPU numbers or explicit deferral note.

title: Route landings by build-graph blast radius
description:
Aviator-style affected-target lanes (Bazel/Nx/Pants/Turborepo/Gradle): classify each change by impacted targets and parallelize landing lanes by blast radius.
Ref: agentic-git-platform-ecosystem-feature-matrix/report.md:59,162
acceptance_criteria: Two changes touching disjoint targets land in parallel lanes; overlapping targets serialize.

title: Agent Office 3D client — deferred/parked by principal (API-consumer only)
description:
Deferred/parked by principal (API-consumer only): John explicitly stopped office effort — 'We want it working in the browser. It's just the 3D Office can be easily integrated into it because it has an API interface.' Zero build effort goes to the 3D client; it plugs in later for free or not at all; browser is the product. SPEC non-goal and queue P3 stand.
Ref: session history 2026-10-04T11:33 user msg; session history 2026-10-04T11:34-11:35 assistant ('office parked, permanently … browser is the product'); SPEC.md:61; docs/NEXT-ACTIONS.md [pending] P3 — Post-submission roadmap
acceptance_criteria: No office work orders unless the principal unpark it; platform API stays client-capable by construction

metadata.check_cmd: bun porting/tasks.mjs list | grep -i 'agent office'

title: Agent Office adapter plan: 5 first integration changes (post-demo)
description:
When/if unparked: (1) Building.add() takes an arbitrary clone URL; (2) a PlatformClient beside gh() constructs Floor.github from platform/CONTRACT.md REST returning the same GhState shape; (3) port the 5 GitHub-API-shaped REST helpers; (4) feed /proposals+conflicts into boards, keep MergeWatch verbatim; (5) map agent sessions to desks via a platform provider and neuter GitHub-only queue links. Zero-GitHub boot is verified.
Ref: /tmp/office-boot/report.md:265-296 (top 5 changes); /tmp/agent-office-analysis/integration-surface.md (H1-H7); /tmp/agent-office-analysis/system-map.md
acceptance_criteria: The office boots against the platform API with no gh binary and renders proposals/conflicts as board state

metadata.check_cmd: read /tmp/office-boot/report.md section 5

title: Signed social graph: follows, stars, permissions as commits
description:
Follows, stars and permissions are signed commits that modify verifiable lists, so the social graph is auditable and forkable like code.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L24-25 (§1 Cryptographic Identity)
acceptance_criteria: Following another user creates a verifiable commit in the follower's social repo; permissions resolve from the signed list.

title: Per-repo actor-model event loops (sharded, isolated actors)
description:
Process repository events (pushes, hooks, actions) in an actor model where every repository is an isolated actor running its own parallel loop, so tenants never share one serialized event queue.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L42 (§2 Radical Parallelization)
acceptance_criteria: An event storm on one repository does not delay event processing for another repository.

title: Federated mirror nodes (ActivityPub + Git), no walled garden
description:
Because identity is cryptographic and data is Git-native, anyone can host a mirror node; if the main instance is down, code, issues and PR histories still push/pull across instances.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L71 (§5 Open Federation)
acceptance_criteria: A mirror serves repository, issue and PR history and re-converges after the origin returns.

title: Live pipeline heatmap for parallel test execution
description:
Show parallel test execution in real time as a visual grid of streaming logs and node clusters so bottlenecks are instantly visible.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L62 (§4 Pipeline Heatmaps)
acceptance_criteria: A running fan-out shows per-node progress and flags the slowest running node.

title: Spatial codebase map: 3D volumes from code metrics
description:
Render a repository as a three-dimensional architectural city: classes and modules are buildings/hubs, height maps to lines of code or complexity and width to function count.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L113-119 (§1 The Spatial Codebase)
acceptance_criteria: A repository renders as an explorable 3D structure whose dimensions derive from real code metrics.

title: Volumetric call-graph traces with request-lifecycle pulses
description:
Functions are nodes inside the 3D structures; calls are glowing volumetric links, and a request animates as a pulse of light traversing the codebase.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L118 (§1 Volumetric Flow)
acceptance_criteria: A traced request highlights the exact 3D path it followed through the code.

title: Structural 3D diff: fissures across dependent downstream models
description:
A pull request isolates the affected 3D structures; breaking an interface shows a visible fissure running through dependent downstream models in real time.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L119 (§1 The Structural Diff)
acceptance_criteria: An interface-breaking change marks downstream dependent structures as broken on the map.

title: 3D volumetric commit history: helix with orbital branches
description:
Turn git log into a navigable 3D timeline or helix: main is the central spine and feature branches spiral outward or orbit the core path.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L123-136 (§2 The 3D Git Commit History)
acceptance_criteria: The history view renders branches as 3D trajectories around a mainline spine.

title: Commit spheres: zoom from macro history into the snapshot
description:
Each commit is an interactable sphere; entering it smoothly zooms from the high-level project history into the microscopic 3D code changes of that snapshot.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L136 (§2 Commit Topology)
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a commit zooms continuously from history scale into its changed structures.

title: Visual merge blending with conflict glow at intersections
description:
Merging two branches animates their geometric paths twisting, intersecting and fusing; conflicting vertices glow amber or red at the exact spatial intersection.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L137 (§2 Visual Merge Blending); L488 (§3 Visual Merge Blending)
acceptance_criteria: Merging branches with a conflict animates the fusion and highlights the conflict vertices.

title: Kinetic pipeline trees: animated CI state on limbs
description:
Visualise parallel CI/CD as an expanding tree whose limbs pulse blue while running, fracture on failure and turn solid green on pass.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L145 (§3 Kinetic Pipeline Trees)
acceptance_criteria: A failing task visibly fractures its limb while passing tasks turn green.

title: Live telemetry overlays: thermal code and traffic currents
description:
Overlay real-time server telemetry onto the codebase model: heavily trafficked code glows like thermal imaging, and enterprise traffic flows render as moving colour-coded currents linking cards.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L146 (§3 Live Traffic Topography); L390; L487 (§3 Kinetic Heatmaps)
acceptance_criteria: Load on an endpoint heats the corresponding code blocks and draws the live flow between services.

title: Avatar-based walkthroughs with spatial audio and comments
description:
Multiple distributed developers inhabit one 3D workspace; seniors walk juniors through the architecture with spatial audio and pin spatial comments directly onto modules.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L150-154 (§4 Immersive Collaborative Environments)
acceptance_criteria: Two users co-inhabit a scene and see each other's pinned spatial comments.

title: Russian-doll nesting mirrors the import tree spatially
description:
Dragging component B inside component A's visual boundary snaps it there, creating a spatial hierarchy that mirrors the actual import tree.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L201 (§1 The Russian Doll Metaphor)
acceptance_criteria: Nesting a node updates the spatial hierarchy and its relationship edges.

title: Inter-component portals synchronise linked views
description:
Open a spatial portal between two related nodes (for example an API endpoint and its frontend consumer); edits made inside the portal sync back to the source node.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L228 (§2 Inter-component Portals)
acceptance_criteria: Editing inside a portal reflects in the linked node across the canvas.

title: Drag-and-drop merging of modified block clusters
description:
Merging a branch or commit is done by grabbing a cluster of modified code blocks from the feature plane and dropping it onto the production layer.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L238 (§3 Interactive Merging via Drag-and-Drop)
acceptance_criteria: Dropping a block cluster stages exactly those changes for merge.

title: WebGPU render loop: thousands of fluid cards at 120 FPS
description:
A custom GPU-accelerated rendering loop treats cards as light graphic objects and keeps interactions at locked 120 FPS even with thousands of open files, bypassing DOM scaling limits.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L244-246 (§4 Rendering Layer)
acceptance_criteria: A stress scene with thousands of live cards holds interactive frame rates.

title: Embed 3D node widgets inside 2D flow nodes (R3F)
description:
Use React Flow for the infinite 2D canvas, panning and edges, while custom nodes host React Three Fiber canvases so connecting nodes alters 3D content inside a flat node.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L290-295 (§1 React Flow + React Three Fiber)
acceptance_criteria: A flow node renders an interactive 3D widget whose properties respond to graph connections.

title: True 3D graph navigation via force-directed layout
description:
For a graph that lives fully in XYZ space with an orbiting camera, use a physics-based 3D force graph as the navigation substrate.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L297-302 (§2 react-force-graph-3d)
acceptance_criteria: A dataset of nodes and links renders as an orbitable 3D graph with physics layout.

title: Nested infinite canvas on a WebGL engine (PixiJS/tldraw)
description:
For an infinite nested canvas where documents physically wrap inside parents, use a WebGL canvas engine that computes camera projection, panning and depth manually.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L304-311 (§3 PixiJS / tldraw)
acceptance_criteria: Deep zoom through nested containers stays fluid beyond DOM element limits.

title: Git as immutable ledger of intention for enterprise state
description:
Every employee, agent, cluster and config string is a discrete node in one global Git graph; infrastructure is a self-evaluating graph rather than a separate hosting environment.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L345-360 (Paradigm Shift: Biological Git Graphs)
acceptance_criteria: An infrastructure change is a graph delta that is reviewable, signable and auditable like code.

title: Micro-state repositories: each infra element its own Git tree
description:
A routing rule, secret key or isolated database instance is its own lightweight self-contained Git tree, so a single config change touches only its micro-repo.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L370-372 (§1 Micro-State Repositories); L470
acceptance_criteria: Editing one routing rule produces a commit only in that element's repository.

title: Cryptographic intention binding between dependent services
description:
Applications declare dependencies through GPG/SSH key bindings and embed the signed hash of the resource they need, so upstream changes ripple only to bound consumers via edge event triggers.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L373 (§1 Cryptographic Mesh Network); L471 (§1 Cryptographic Intention Binding)
acceptance_criteria: A dependency update propagates only to consumers whose signed bindings match.

title: Service mesh compiled to edge KV within milliseconds
description:
Compile every routing-table change to deterministic key-value pairs propagated across Cloudflare's edge so network topology morphs as fast as agents commit.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L472 (§1 Decentralized Service Mesh via Cloudflare KV)
acceptance_criteria: A routing commit updates global edge behaviour within a measured interval and with no central control-plane query.

title: Semantic zoom of the enterprise matrix
description:
Top layer shows the company as interacting galaxies of business units; zooming in reveals regions, service meshes, applications, and finally the line being edited.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L388 (§3 Semantic Zooming of the Enterprise Matrix); L486
acceptance_criteria: One zoom traversal goes company, region, service, application, line.

title: Dynamic clustering of failing services on the canvas
description:
Services under heavy traffic or security failure physically expand and highlight red, pulling spatial attention from automated agents or engineers.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L389 (§3 Dynamic Structural Clustering); L487
acceptance_criteria: An induced failure enlarges and marks the affected service on the canvas.

title: Autonomous optimization swarms acting on live telemetry
description:
Specialised agent swarms watch telemetry, fork the affected micro-state repo, optimise the logic, verify on the Wasm grid and auto-merge the patch.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L397 (§4 Autonomous Optimization Swarms); L495
acceptance_criteria: A seeded bottleneck yields an autonomous optimisation patch with validation evidence.

title: CRDT consensus with priority rules for overlapping agents
description:
Thousands of concurrent overlapping edits merge mathematically by logical priority rules instead of branch locks, with deltas committed to regional nodes and resolved globally.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L398 (§4 Conflict Resolution via CRDT Consensus); L496; L667
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping concurrent deltas merge deterministically with no lock queue and no stuck branch.

title: Unified distributed DAG of cryptographically signed nodes
description:
Code, routing, compute limits, dependencies and agent intentions unify as signed nodes in one fluid distributed DAG that is the enterprise.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L435 (The Self-Synthesizing Enterprise)
acceptance_criteria: Any node's provenance and dependency bindings are verifiable from the graph alone.

title: Account mesh: millions of Durable Object coordinate nodes
description:
Treat an account as a self-routing, globally distributed mesh of Durable Object coordinate nodes rather than a row in a database.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L627-638 (§1 The Autonomous Account Mesh)
acceptance_criteria: An account scales regionally with no central account-wide lock or identity hotspot.

title: Spatial sharding: run state nearest the active entity
description:
Durable Objects distribute to the data centre closest to each active human or agent, so one account's state fractures and runs regionally in parallel with async mesh routing.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L638 (§1 The Spatial Sharding Engine)
acceptance_criteria: Two regions process concurrently without cross-region serialisation.

title: Ephemeral regional secret injection via authorization tree
description:
Never replicate credentials to all nodes: inject keys at the regional edge layer transiently, single-session and need-to-know, validated by localised handshakes.
Ref: Redesigning-GitHub-With-Git-Architecture (2).md L639 (§1 Decoupled Multi-Tier Security Profiles)
acceptance_criteria: A secret is usable for exactly one session in one region and is never replicated further.

title: Revision-centric VCS with effortless stacking and rewriting
description:
Adopt a jj-style revision-centric model where every working-copy change is automatically a commit, making stacking, reordering and splitting changes first-class operations without corruption risk.

acceptance_criteria: Reordering and splitting changes works as undoable first-class operations on a working copy.

title: Reveal secret values only through an authorized, audited seam rule
description: New seam-gated reveal path: `POST /reveal {repo, ref, path, key}` behind `authorize(request, env, "reveal", {repo})` with an explicit authorization rule (identity allowlist + repo scope config, e.g. `REVEAL_ALLOW`; default = no one), additive CONTRACT.md bump for request/response/error shapes. Denied ⇒ `403 {ok:false,error:"reveal-not-authorized"}` with no value; every grant AND denial writes a content-free audit record (identity, repo, path, key, decision, at — never the value, never in logs). The value is read from the Artifacts blob for the secret-class path only when authorized. No other route or view gains a value surface: schema-only rows + the withheld notice remain the complete default surface, and the masking law (CONTRACT "Secret classes") is untouched. Depends on the seam and the §7.5 auth decision gate (FR-31 sequencing: no value-reveal surface ships before the seam is enforced). Overlap: `elevated-reveal-for-authorized-viewers-demo-beat` [pending P2] is the umbrella demo-beat row — this story is the seam-backed authorization-rule + audit delta.
acceptance_criteria: Exact copy (FR-31): "Elevated reveal requires the auth seam plus an explicit authorization rule; until then it does not exist anywhere in the product." and "No route or view exposes secret-class values today; the schema-only view and the withheld notice are the complete surface." With AUTH_MODE=deny or an unauthorized identity, every reveal attempt is 401/403 with no value in the body or logs; with an authorized identity (test stub), the requested key's value is returned and an audit record is written for the grant; a denial also writes an audit record; every other route's responses still contain no secret-class value.

title: Fail closed on blob integrity checks at every materialization path
description: R2 asset tier read path. Build one verified-materialization chokepoint in the tier's module (`platform/src/assets.ts`, or the module the first-slice row `r2-asset-tier-manifest-format` lands — conform, never fork the format): `readVerifiedBlob(env, blobId, expectedSha256)` fetches the object via the asset-bucket R2 binding (name pinned by the first slice; wired in `platform/wrangler.jsonc`, typed bindings regenerated with `wrangler types` into `platform/worker-configuration.d.ts`), recomputes SHA-256 over the exact bytes, and returns them only when the digest equals both the content-addressed blob id and the pointer's recorded content hash. Mismatch — tampered object, substituted key, or pointer/content divergence — throws a typed `BlobIntegrityError` and materializes nothing. Every site that can return blob bytes must call the chokepoint: the asset download route in `platform/src/index.ts`, any clone/checkout materialization hook, and future presigned-confirmation paths; no byte-returning `bucket.get(...)` exists outside it. Route boundary maps the error to a non-2xx `{ok:false,error:"integrity"}` body per the tier's contract (bump `platform/CONTRACT.md` first when a new route/response shape lands — contract-first, FR-42). No partial content, no fallback to another object/key, never cache or serve unverified bytes; log the mismatch with pointer path and expected/actual digest only (no blob content; AD-4 / NFR-5).
acceptance_criteria: Given a stored blob whose bytes hash to H and a pointer recording content hash H, when a read materializes it, then the exact bytes are returned. Given a stored object whose bytes no longer hash to the pointer's content hash (or to its content-addressed key) after tampering or substitution, when any read path materializes it, then the read fails closed: `BlobIntegrityError` at the module boundary and a non-2xx `{ok:false,error:"integrity"}` at the route — zero bytes returned, no silent substitution, no fallback. Both mismatch directions are covered by tests: pointer hash != stored digest, and blob id key != stored digest. The source tree has exactly one byte-returning read of the asset bucket (the chokepoint; grep-verified) and the test drives both the module and the route handler through it. The mismatch log line contains no blob content.

title: Delete asset pointers lifecycle-safely with bucket rules and no orphan blobs
description: Lifecycle half of the tier. (1) Bucket lifecycle rules: commit the asset bucket's retention/expiry configuration as `platform/r2-lifecycle.json` and apply it with the lockfile-pinned wrangler (`cd platform && ./node_modules/.bin/wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle set <asset-bucket> r2-lifecycle.json`); `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle list <asset-bucket>` must show the committed rules; record the bucket name plus apply command in the platform tier doc/README when the first slice pins the bucket. (2) Reference-aware, lifecycle-safe deletes: a repo path removal is a normal file delete (the pointer disappears with the commit/fold). After the platform's write path (`/land` in `platform/src/land.ts` + `platform/src/index.ts`) folds removals, each removed pointer's blob is checked against the union of every repo's pointer manifests (Artifacts listing; source of truth is the repo manifests — any cache/index must be rebuildable from them) and is deleted/scheduled only when its reference count is zero. Shared blobs are never deleted while any repo or path still references them. Per-request work stays inside the 30 s CPU envelope (NFR-1): the land path checks only blobs touched by the fold; bulk reclamation is out-of-band. (3) Orphan audit + sweep: `platform/scripts/r2-orphan-sweep.mjs` lists bucket keys, subtracts the union of manifest-referenced blob ids across all repos, reports orphans, deletes those older than a grace window, and exits non-zero if any orphan remains after the sweep; it runs from the repo root using the same API-token resolution as `platform/scripts/fanout.mjs`.
acceptance_criteria: Given manifests where path a points to blobX and no other repo or path references blobX, when path a is removed through the normal commit/fold path, then the pointer is gone and blobX is scheduled/deleted (reference count zero). Given blobX is still referenced from another repo or path, when a is removed, then blobX survives — no shared-blob deletion. Given a bucket containing an unreferenced blob older than the grace window, when the sweep runs, then it deletes it and a follow-up audit reports zero orphans; a fresh unreferenced blob inside the grace window is reported but not deleted. Given the deployed asset bucket, when `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle list` runs, then the committed retention/expiry rules are present. No request path performs an unbounded bucket scan (NFR-1).
